Wizz Air has said it swung to a loss in an “extremely volatile” period following the Middle East conflict which has sent fuel costs soaring.

The low-cost airline warned that the industry is set to face challenges for the rest of the year.

It recorded an operating loss of 183 million euros (£157 million) between April and June, down from a profit of 27.5 million euros (£23.6 million) for the same period last year.

Wizz said this largely reflected a jump in jet fuel costs, linked to the increase in global oil prices – with Brent crude oil peaking above 120 dollars a barrel in late April.

Its fuel expenses jumped by 39% compared with last year, to 610.5 million euros (£523.8 million).

The airline said this reflected 87% higher market prices, which it managed to partially mitigate through its own cost actions.

The increased expenses for jet fuel have slammed the industry, with easyJet, British Airways owner IAG and Ryanair all reporting a fall in profits in recent weeks.

Wizz previously said it took a 50 million euro (£42.9 million) hit from the Iran war after having to cancel flights to Tel Aviv in Israel and other routes to the Middle East and Cyprus in March.

While many flights have resumed, the company said it was reallocating flying from longer-haul Middle East routes to shorter European markets.

The weaker earnings update came despite its passenger numbers soaring by a quarter to 21.2 million over the three-month period.

Total revenues also increased by 5.5% year-on-year to 1.5 billion euros (£1.29 billion).

Chief executive Jozsef Varadi said: “The industry has been extremely volatile over the June quarter due to conflict in the Middle East, elevated fuel prices, and changes in booking patterns.

“We are focused on strengthening the core network, improving density and reallocating flying from longer-haul Middle Eastern operations into shorter European sectors.

“While we continue to see the build-up of forward bookings, the rest of the year is expected to present both industry challenges and strategic opportunities.”

News.title: ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality
News.content:
Arsenal 1 Real Betis 3

Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

But that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the new season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he said.

“We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

“All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”

Despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. When asked about the mood in the dressing room, he said: “Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”

Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

No Saliba a concern

The importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

Raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

Only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” said Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

News.title: Ebola outbreak outpacing containment effort, WHO chief warns
News.content:
Caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, for which there are no vaccines or treatments, it has been extremely difficult to contain, according to experts on the ground.

“The outbreak is spreading faster than our scale-up of the response, with new cases doubling in some hotspots over the past week alone,” Dr Tedros said on X.

Part of the difficulty is that the virus was circulating undetected for weeks before the outbreak was formally declared in mid-May, leaving health officials even now racing to catch up with the spread.

Prof Placide Mbala, director of research, clinical trials and innovation at Africa CDC, told the Telegraph: “It’s mostly the fact we arrived a bit late. It took us some time before we detected this virus outbreak. And when we detected the outbreak, we already had a total of I can say more than 200 suspected cases. It’s been difficult to catch up. That’s where we are.”

While the DRC has a wealth of experience in tackling haemorrhagic fever outbreaks, the effects of that initial delay are still being felt.

Prof Mbala said: “We have some experience dealing with the cases, the labs, the communication, the infection prevention and control.

“We have some experience... But my observation is that we were very slow, and it’s why we’re in this situation.

“We are slow detecting the people, slow responding, we are slow deploying people, we are slow to recruit the community healthcare workers to improve contact tracing, we are slow to deploy the safe burials.”

DRC’s largest outbreak had previously been from 2018 to 2020, when 3,481 cases were recorded.

The West Africa outbreak recorded 28,616 cases and 11,310 deaths according to the WHO.

Prof Mbala said insecurity was also severely hampering attempts to curb the virus. The outbreak epicentre is in Ituri province, which has been wracked by ethnic strife for decades and is also home to militias competing to control mining.

He said: “There are many, many mining groups controlling most of the mining places. We have a big issue with those places, because they are places where the response team cannot go.”

Medics and aid workers have also been undermined by violent public distrust of their efforts.

Locals in the area have either doubted the existence of the virus, or have accused health teams of deliberately spreading the infection, or somehow benefiting from it.

More than a dozen health facilities have been set alight and several health workers have been killed.

Prof Mbala said: “The local people, they also sometimes are very upset, because they believe that it’s a kind of a business, and people who are coming here, they are getting a lot of money, [so] don’t want this disease to stop.”

He said he hoped that immunity was starting to rise in some areas and this would start to curb transmission.

However there was also a risk that people fleeing the outbreak would spread the virus further afield.

He said: “The second scenario is the fact we are seeing people moving from the affected area to new areas, to run away from the response team because they do not want to go to the treatment centre.

“And in complicity with their family members living in other areas, they are now the ones who are spreading the disease to new areas

“So we’ll see new places affected because people are moving around from the affected zone to the non-affected zone.”

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

News.title: Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat
News.content:
Chelsea 0 Juventus 1

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

News.title: The underground lab where ‘princess mosquitoes’ are treated like royalty
News.content:
Beneath the grand Art Deco headquarters of the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine lies a vast labyrinth inhabited by weird and wonderful creatures.

In this maze of subterranean labs, store rooms and corridors live colonies of disease-bearing insects and arachnids from all over the world, from bed bugs, sand flies and microscopic dust mites to the so-called kissing bugs that spread Chagas disease – a sinister condition that can cause its victims to drop dead of heart failure without warning, albeit decades after the first (silent) infection.

Behind a series of doors, contained in stacks of mesh boxes, you can even find the flies that spread trachoma, the Dickensian eye disease that is still a leading cause of blindness around the world. But be warned: entering the room is not for the faint of heart – the flies feed on human excrement and the smell is impossible to forget.

There are also many varieties of mosquito, including several species of the Anopheles genus that spread malaria, Culex and Aedes mosquitoes that are also vectors for human and animal diseases, and even Toxorhynchites, perhaps better known as the elephant mosquito, a friendly giant which doesn’t bite people but preys on other mosquitoes.

These animals have been studied intensely since the insectaries were established in the building’s vaults in the 1960s, underpinning many breakthroughs in the control, surveillance, and understanding of vector-borne diseases in the developing world.

LSHTM researchers are now looking closer to home. They have established the UK’s first laboratory colony of Aedes vexans mosquitoes, a species native to the British isles, to study whether they could harbour diseases like West Nile virus, Rift Valley fever, Zika or Japanese encephalitis.

News.title: What I saw in a week on the front line of Afghanistan’s hunger crisis
News.content:
May 15 and 16, 2026

It is the weekend, a small moment to rest, although there is still a lot of work waiting for me. A week in the field does not mean that work in Kabul stops. I try to catch up on my emails and have a planned online interview for an international staff position – since in Europe, Friday is a normal working day. I also review parts of new proposals for donors and our financial planning.

On Saturday, however, I take a short break. Together with the base management team in Helmand, we visit a historical site called Qala-e-Bost, believed to have been built around 3,000 years ago. It is a rare moment to step away from work, followed by lunch with the team.

May 17, 2026

Sunday morning, the first working day of the week, we visit Basrhan Sub Health Centre, run by one of our local partners. As a nurse and former nurse trainer, I feel very much in my element in these health centres. It allows me to engage easily with the team and discuss their work.

I speak with the outreach officer and the vaccinator. They explain that this facility supports 18 outreach locations, each visited at least once a month. They provide vaccinations, raise awareness, and connect communities to the health centre. These visits often take place in simple settings, like mosques.

Immunisation is now well accepted. In the beginning, there was some resistance, but trust has grown over time. Every child is tracked, and if a child misses a vaccination, community health volunteers follow up at home. For extra polio vaccinations, this is carefully recorded by marking a finger of the child – helping ensure that no child is missed. The goal is clear: a polio-free Afghanistan.

I also speak with a mother. She is wearing a burka, so I cannot see her face. She tells me she is 22 years old and holds her 12-month-old son on her lap. She came because he has a fever, but I see a healthy child – something that stands out after my time in the TFU.

She brings her child regularly for follow-up and growth monitoring and the child has never been in a treatment program for malnutrition. She speaks positively about the services. “We are lucky,” she says. “The staff treat us well, and we have access to care in our community.”

News.title: World’s first seahorse hospital fights to protect them from extinction
News.content:
With careful precision, marine biologist Linda Albonetti extracts a 10cm-long injured seahorse – a heavily pregnant male – from an aquarium tank to apply healing ointment to its wound.

Linda, 29, coordinator at the world’s first specialist seahorse hospital, is currently caring for around 50 of these tiny creatures, all of which were brought in by local fishing crews after becoming snagged in their nets.

The seahorse will be kept for a few more days before it is released back into the Adriatic Sea, giving it time to recover from the cut to the soft, bony plates that form its outer carapace.

What the team here are doing is a literal drop in the ocean, a small attempt to fight back against the potential extinction of these remarkable fish.

In Europe and around countries like Indonesia, they are being poached in their millions for sale to a voracious Asian traditional medicine market where they are consumed as an aphrodisiac and alleged cure for impotence, asthma and kidney problems.

“There is definitely a downward trend in the overall seahorse population because they are being collected for the Asian market,” says Linda. “Technically, they cannot be exported to countries such as China, but there is no specific law preventing that trade. They do not have the same protections as sea turtles, for example.

“It is not happening in this part of Italy yet, but it is further south, off the Mediterranean coast. That is why it is so important that we monitor their numbers and maintain a good relationship with the local fishermen.”

News.title: The 13 best castle hotels in England
News.content:
Few places capture the imagination quite like a castle, and England is home to some of the most remarkable places to spend the night. If it’s not the romance of waking up in a canopied four-poster bed, or losing ourselves in centuries-old tapestries and visceral oil paintings, we are lured by tales of brave knights and plotting dignitaries, duplicitous royals and ghosts parleying secrets in the hallways.

Part of the magic is spending an afternoon wandering grounds and gardens followed by evenings in front of a roaring fire, or dining in a banquet hall that may have hosted medieval kings and queens. While not every castle has crenellated battlements, glistening moats or royal connections, each stony stronghold on our list has something special that makes it worth travelling for. In this modern age that might include a spa, fine-dining restaurant or extra touches like free admission to exhibitions and museum tours. Here’s our pick of the best castle hotels in England.

News.title: Careless Liverpool concede same goal twice in second-half capitulation against Leeds
News.content:
Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. Sports.title: Fifa caught sending pre-signed ‘scripted letters’ to secure Gianni Infantino re-election as ‘blackmail’ crisis worsens
Sports.content:
FIFA reportedly issued scripted letters to football federations that provided wording to endorse president Gianni Infantino for re-election.

Infantino is under immense pressure to resign as head of football’s governing body after his failed attempt to sell off chunks of the World Cup to private investors.



The Swiss chief, 56, attended an emergency crisis meeting in Morocco after angering the world of football with his plans.

He remains in charge after the crisis meeting and has vowed to fight on at Fifa ahead of next year’s presidential elections on March 18, 2027.



And according to Sky News, Fifa sent out scripted letters to football associations in a bid to drum up support for the elections.

It is said to have included words praising Infantino’s work at the organisation over the last decade.



The report claims the name and signature of the relevant FA chief was provided on the letter, which was intended to be returned to Fifa.

SunSport has approached Fifa for comment.

Fifa’s governance regulations do not ban the use of internal resources for election campaigns.

They state: “Candidatures and electoral campaigns shall be carried out by the candidates in a fair and reputable manner and, more generally, in a spirit of respect for fundamental ethical principles and FIFA regulations.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“Candidates shall conduct all campaigns with dignity and moderation and with respect for any other candidate(s), for FIFA itself and for its member associations.”

Earlier this month it was claimed by the Guardian that more than 200 Fifa members had endorsed Infantino for the election.

But in light of Infantino’s plot to set up subsidiary Fifa Forward Enterprise, which would run the World Cup and be open to private investment, he is losing support rapidly.

Uefa threatened a boycott of the World Cup before the plan was axed and have withdrawn their support, along with the FA and the Welsh FA.



It’s understood Uefa are preparing a candidate to run against Infantino ahead of the November 18 deadline amid reports their president Alexander Ceferin could stand.

It comes after Infantino apologised over Fifa’s controversial World Cup scheme, admitting mistakes were made.

In a joint letter signed by Infantino and secretary general Mattias Grafstrom, senior officials said: “We sincerely apologise for these errors and commit to them not happening again.

Sports.title: Bombshell documents expose Fifa boss Infantino’s undercover partnership to launch rival Super League and sideline clubs
Sports.content:
BOMBSHELL documents exposed Gianni Infantino plotted to partner with the breakaway European Super League.

And it was even proposed to name it the ‘Fifa Super League’.



News broke in April 2021 of the 20-team league proposed to shake up club football.

Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool, Manchester City, Manchester United and Tottenham all signed up to the closed-shop division.



It would have created a new rival competition featuring 15 permanent members – also including co-founders Real Madrid, Barcelona, Atletico, Inter Milan, AC Milan and Juventus – and five qualifying teams.

But intense, furious backlash to the plans from excluded teams, football governing bodies and fans across the world saw the Super League collapse and scrapped.



At the time, Fifa president Infantino told Uefa’s congress that his organisation condemned the proposed new league.

He said: “At Fifa, we can only strongly disapprove the creation of a Super League which is a closed shop, which is a breakaway from the current institutions, from the leagues, from the associations, from Uefa and from Fifa, which is outside of the system.

“There is no doubt whatsoever of Fifa’s disapproval for this.”

However, according to The Guardian, shocking files now allege he was very much part of the breakaway rebellion.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The report claims a term sheet – usually a precurser to a ratified and definitive contract – dated in October 2020 suggests naming the new league with Fifa’s branding.

The Guardian also suggests Fifa were willing to sideline its member associations in pushing plans to alter international windows and bypassed federations over Club World Cup proposals.

The Club World Cup would have been staged annually and directly connected to the new Super League.

And the damning documents, according to The Guardian, suggest Fifa are referred to as ‘WO1’ – a term used for high-ranking officers in the British army.



The report explains the term sheet said the Super League “is open to discuss naming the competition WO1 SL”.

It also stated Fifa would be “granted a preferred equity stake in the Super League”, thus ensuring the power to make decisions on format and calendar changes plus the appointment of a chief executive and distribution of funds.

When approached by SunSport for comment, Fifa sent links to articles posted in 2021 including Infantino’s comments to the Uefa congress and a signed statement from the Fifa boss plus the presidents of the six continental confederations refusing to recognise any unafiliated, rival competitions.

The outlandish expose comes a week after Infantino’s plans to auction off stakes in the World Cup were made public.

The angry reaction from confederations, national FAs and even many within Fifa prompted a swift and embarrassing U-turn for the Swiss chief, who is now desperately clinging on to power after a humiliating week.



He is holed up in Rabat, Morocco, where he staged an emergency crisis meeting with Fifa big-wigs.

Infantino apologised but vowed to fight on as the head of world football.

Further reports – denied by Fifa – suggest Infantino has offered Morocco the World Cup final in 2030 in return for public backing, as he still awaits support from 2034 hosts Saudi Arabia.

Meanwhile, Portugal legend Luis Figo tweeted on Wednesday: “Today I join others from across our game and call for Gianni Infantino to resign as Fifa President.

“Infantino has debased the office that he promised to elevate.



“He has lied, deceived and tried to feather his own nest at the expense of the game he is supposed to serve.

“He has lost the support of his senior staff, his closest advisers, the vast majority of people who devote their lives to this sport and even, it would seem, the Fifa Peace Prize winner.

“It is too late to save his dignity but it is not too late to save football. He should go. Now. #Infantinout”

That came 24 hours after the Jordan FA boss Prince Ali Bin Al Hussein accused Infantino and Fifa of “blackmail”.

Prince Ali wrote: “There is no shortage of issues regarding Fifa.



“We have been waiting for reward money for our players since December for the Arab Cup in Qatar, which is a Fifa event.

“The money our team should receive for having reached the final has not been delivered yet, while at the same time Fifa brags about how many billions they have in reserve.

“It is clear the problem really is with leadership.

“For months, Fifa has been refusing to help us on any of these or other matters – until it was verbally communicated to me during the World Cup that if I endorsed Infantino it would go a long way to helping our FA out.

“We pride ourselves in Jordan in upholding ethical values.



“We did not endorse him before and certainly will not now.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“But the whole situation amounts to blackmail and we refuse to give in to that.”

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Talks with Trabzonspor accelerated this week and led to the winger flying in from Greek island Mykonos.

It was at the airport there where the 34-year-old was mobbed by fans, who set off flares and fireworks.

Mohamed Salah is "too good" to be playing for Trabzonspor and should have stayed in a top European league after leaving Liverpool, according to Jamie Carragher. Salah is poised to sign a two-year deal with the Turkish side after being mobbed by excited fans at the airport on Wednesday.

‌



Salah is a free agent after walking away from Liverpool - and his £400,000-a-week contract - at the end of last season. He has ended up in the north of Turkey, where he will play for the side which finished third in the Super Lig last season.

‌



Trabzonspor, who have Manchester United loanee Andre Onana in goal, last won the title in 2022 and will play in the Europa League next season. They have won the race to sign Salah, who will be officially unveiled on Thursday evening, having already been given a seismic welcome by thousands of fans at Ataturk Airport in Istanbul and then later at Trabzon Airport.

‌



There had been speculation that the 34-year-old would end up in Saudi Arabia, due to his sky-high wage demands. But Carragher is disappointed he didn't end up in Italy, where he could have continued to play at a high level and prolong his career like Cristiano Ronaldo.

Liverpool exploring Ibrahim Mbaye transfer as PSG star's stance on move emerges READ MORE :

"I never believed he was going to go to Saudi, because number one, he's too good for that. I think he can be playing in Serie A. Turkey for me feels a level too low," he told the Football Ramble.

‌



"I was convinced he'd end up at an AC Milan or Juventus or somewhere like that, maybe his wages were a problem. Looking at him, I don't know him, obviously have never spoken to him.

"But he's like Ronaldo, he's so driven, his numbers mean so much to him. I thought, he can still do this in Turkey by the way, but I thought he'd want to play at a real prestigious club."

View 2 Images Mohamed Salah got a hero's welcome at Trabzon Airport (Image: Hakan Burak Altunoz/Anadolu via Getty Images)

‌



Salah's wages were always likely to be a barrier for interested clubs and it seems the Egyptian was an unrealistic signing for many big clubs. While Trabzonspor haven't had to pay a transfer fee, they have completely altered their wage structure to make the biggest signing in their history.

"Obviously his wage demands have put a few people off but I thought he might almost curb those demands a little bit to almost get a better club," Carragher added.

"To go to an AC Milan or Juventus or whoever it may be, play at the San Siro, still playing in big games, still playing in Europe. Turkey just feels like... I just think he's better than that."

Article continues below

Salah will now embark upon a new stage of his career after leaving behind Liverpool, where he scored 257 goals in 442 appearances over nine years and won two Premier League titles, the Champions League, the Club World Cup, the UEFA Super Cup, FA Cup and two Carabao Cups.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta gives blunt response to Bruno Guimaraes question after Newcastle transfer agreed
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta gives blunt response to Bruno Guimaraes question after Newcastle transfer agreed

Arsenal are poised to announce the signing of Bruno Guimaraes in a £75million deal from Newcastle in a significant boost which comes after a friendly defeat by Real Betis

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta spoke after a friendly defeat by Real Betis (Image: Charles McQuillan/Getty Images)

Mikel Arteta kept his cards close to his chest when asked about the impending arrival of Bruno Guimaraes at Arsenal following their friendly loss against Real Betis.

‌



The Gunners were beaten 3-1 by their Spanish opponents on Wednesday night in a disappointing performance. Piero Hincapie's header from a corner was the only consolation for Arteta's side, who appeared rusty in Dublin.

‌



Arsenal have been relatively quiet in the summer transfer window so far, with a £34million deal for Christos Tzolis and a free transfer for Illan Meslier the only major done deals. But they are soon to be boosted by the arrival of Guimaraes, who is set to undergo his medical in the coming days after a £75m fee was agreed with Newcastle.

‌



The Brazil international is due in north London after leaving Newcastle's pre-season training camp in Spain and will replace Christian Norgaard, who joined Everton for £7m. The deal was agreed on Wednesday before Arsenal's defeat by Betis, but Arteta would not discuss it.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Vinicius Jr takes extreme measures amid Arsenal transfer interest and Real Madrid meeting READ MORE :

How Arsenal could line up after signing Bruno Guimaraes and completing Vinicius Jr transfer READ MORE :

"I'm not going to talk about any players who aren't Arsenal players," he said when first asked in his post-match press conference.

‌



When pressed, he added: "Well, I can tell you at the moment that something happens and we can announce it. I will give you my straight answer."

While he won't yet say it, Guimaraes' arrival will come as a significant boost for Arsenal. The 28-year-old has 30 goals and 26 assists in 153 Premier League appearances for Newcastle and will add competition for places and leadership in midfield.

It is understood that he has had his heart set on Arsenal since hearing of their interest and his insistence forced Newcastle to sell. Arsenal initially offered £60m, while the Magpies wanted £80m for their captain, who had two years left on his contract. A compromise was reached at £75m.

‌



View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes will soon be an Arsenal player (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Once Guimaraes has joined, Arsenal will turn their attention to signing a centre-back and another attacker. William Saliba's back injury has forced the Gunners into the market, with Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa a key target. However, the England international has two years left on his deal and is valued at £60m by Villa.

Meanwhile, a move for Vinicius Junior hangs in the balance, with Real Madrid in delicate negotiations to try and extend his contract. Vinicius' current deal expires in June 2027 and he wants a pay increase to bring him closer to Kylian Mbappe's level.

Article continues below

Real are understood to have offered him an increase, but short of what the 26-year-old Brazilian was looking for. It remains to be seen if a compromise can be reached, but while Vinicius has raised eyebrows by deleting his Instagram posts, he has not stated a desire to leave this summer.

Sports.title: Liverpool could lose TEN players for nothing as they fail to learn their transfer lesson
Sports.content:
Liverpool could lose TEN players for nothing as they fail to learn their transfer lesson

Liverpool could suffer a massive loss in squad depth if they repeat past mistakes

View 3 Images Liverpool have plenty of work to if they want to keep several stars at Anfield (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

Despite Liverpool’s knack for recouping solid funds on fringe talent, their broader strategy around expiring contracts has cost them dearly. The Reds have had numerous successes in regards to player sales in the past, having previously sold the likes of Rhian Brewster for £23.5million and Sepp van den Berg for £25m.

‌



While they successfully leveraged £10m out of Real Madrid for Trent Alexander-Arnold by taking advantage of Madrid's eagerness to register him before the Club World Cup, their high-profile exits tell a much harsher story.

‌



Under the stewardship of Arne Slot, Andy Robertson, Ibrahima Konate and Mohamed Salah - who mutually agreed to rip up the last year of his deal - all departed the club for nothing this summer.

‌



The trio's exits could have resulted in a windfall if the Reds had learned from the free transfer departures of Roberto Firmino, Georginio Wijnaldum, and Emre Can in the past. The pattern may well be repeating itself with 10 first-team players currently poised to walk away for nothing next summer, unless contract renewals are agreed.

Virgil van Dijk, Alisson Becker, Curtis Jones, Harvey Elliott, Joe Gomez, Wataru Endo, Kostas Tsimikas, Stefan Bajcetic, Calvin Ramsay and Harvey Davies could all be experiencing their final campaign at Anfield.

Mohamed Salah agrees two-year deal with new club after emotional Liverpool exit READ MORE :

Virgil van Dijk transfer lined up as club chiefs 'gutted' at missed Liverpool opportunity READ MORE :

Reds captain Van Dijk will turn 36 years old a week after his deal runs out next June, yet remains an enormously influential presence at the club. Van Dijk clocked up the most minutes in Europe last season and it's still uncertain whether he'll be handed an extension on his £350,000-a-week terms.

‌



He's a prime target for MLS outfit Chicago Fire, who recently completed the capture of Robert Lewandowski. It did seem for a period that Liverpool supporters might have bid farewell to Alisson, with the Brazilian shot-stopper attracting attention from Juventus.

View 3 Images Joe Gomez, Harvey Elliott and Kostas Tsimikas have entered the last year of their contracts (Image: Getty Images)

Nevertheless, the 33-year-old chose to honour the final year of his Liverpool deal and could pursue a return to Serie A next summer or spend his latter years with boyhood side Internacional.

‌



Curtis Jones' future has been a persistent topic of discussion this summer as Inter Milan have repeatedly chased a move for the 25-year-old. Following a rejected £21m approach for the midfielder, the Serie A champions have approached the Reds regarding a £30m transaction, as reported by the ECHO.

Fellow midfielder Harvey Elliott has returned to Anfield following a disastrous loan stint at Aston Villa last season. The 23-year-old has been afforded an opportunity to impress Andoni Iraola this summer, as the Reds' shortage of options in midfield and attack could provide him with the chance to cement his place in the squad once more.

View 3 Images Alisson Becker and Wataru Endo could be playing their last season with the Reds (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

‌



Poised to begin his 12th campaign as a Liverpool player, Joe Gomez is the club's longest-serving member of the squad. The 28-year-old's persistent injury problems have meant he hasn't been dependable and is due to miss the opening of the season after sustaining a muscle injury in the Reds' first pre-season fixture against Sunderland.

Next summer could be the moment when Gomez and the club go their separate ways, but a return to Anfield will be arranged for his testimonial. Kostas Tsimikas will resume his previous position of backup left-back this season, after a disappointing season-long loan at Roma.

The Greek international, 30, acknowledged he's "really happy" to be back on Merseyside and will probably be afforded plenty of chances to prolong his stay at Liverpool, with the club involved in four competitions.

Sports.title: Arsenal's 17 Brazilian stars ranked as Bruno Guimaraes deal nears – from Wellington Silva to Edu
Sports.content:
Arsenal's 17 Brazilian stars ranked as Bruno Guimaraes deal nears – from Wellington Silva to Edu

Bruno Guimaraes is set to follow a long line of Brazilians in joining Arsenal, though many of his predecessors failed to hit the mark in N5

View 7 Images Bruno Guimaraes is set to join Arsenal from Newcastle (Image: Getty)

Bruno Guimaraes is all set to become an Arsenal player after Gunners bosses finally reached a breakthrough with Newcastle United following several weeks of negotiations. The Premier League champions will sign the 28-year-old after agreeing a £75million deal.

‌



With personal terms long finalised and the midfielder granted permission to undergo his medical ahead of signing a five-year contract, Mikel Arteta is on the verge of landing his top target to reinforce the Gunners' engine room.

‌



When the Selecao star officially puts pen to paper, he will become the latest addition in a long and rich line of Brazilian talent plying their trade in the red half of north London. Arsenal's samba connection stretches back to the Arsene Wenger era and has remained strong throughout Arteta's tenure.

‌



Guimaraes arrives with massive expectations, following in the footsteps of compatriots who came before him, ranging from legendary Gunners figures to forgettable panic signings and fizzled-out youth prospects. Here, Mirror Football ranks all 17 Brazilians who have signed for Arsenal.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arsenal set to agree blockbuster Bruno Guimaraes transfer as Newcastle demands finally met READ MORE :

Ex-Arsenal star makes winning return to English football with League Two club READ MORE :

17 - Pedro Botelho

Signed from Figueirense in 2007, persistent work-permit issues meant he spent his entire Arsenal spell shipped out on loan to various Spanish clubs. He departed in 2012 without ever making a single official senior appearance.

‌



16 - Wellington Silva

View 7 Images Wellington Silva didn't play an official game for the club (Image: Getty)

Arrived as a highly rated teenager in 2010 but work-permit restrictions forced him through five separate loan spells before he could officially feature in England. He eventually returned to Fluminense in 2016, leaving north London without playing a competitive first-team match.

15 - Juan

The left-back joined from Sao Paulo in 2001 but made just two appearances before a cruel knee injury halted his progress. He quietly headed back to Brazil in 2004 without ever getting the chance to launch his Gunners career.

‌



14 - Neto

You would be forgiven for forgetting the goalkeeper ever played for Arsenal. Brought in on loan from Bournemouth in August 2024 to provide experienced cover for David Raya between the posts. The veteran keeper made a solitary appearance in the Champions League before returning to his parent club at the end of the season.

13 - Marquinhos

One of Edu's signings, the young winger showed immediate promise by scoring and assisting on a dream Europa League debut against FC Zurich in 2022 after signing from Sao Paulo. However, he struggled to establish a permanent role in Arteta's plans and spent much of his time on loan away from the club before signing permanently for Cruzeiro in 2025.

‌



12 - Willian

View 7 Images Willian struggled in his only season at Arsenal (Image: Visionhaus)

Willian controversially arrived on a lucrative free transfer from Chelsea in 2020 but failed to reproduce his Stamford Bridge form in north London. After a miserable single season featuring just one goal in 37 outings, the best thing the veteran winger did was agree to tear up his contract and leave on good terms.

11 - Andre Santos

Andre Santos was signed in 2011 to plug a hole at left-back, offering plenty of attacking intent and memorable goals against Chelsea and West Brom. However, defensive frailties and an infamous half-time shirt swap with Robin van Persie made his stay short-lived. These days, memories of Santos are largely limited to memes, with some of his useful contributions being overshadowed.

‌



10 - Gabriel Paulista

Joined from Villarreal in 2015, bringing intense passion and aggressive defending to the Arsenal backline across 64 appearances. He picked up two FA Cup winners' medals during his two-and-a-half-year stay before returning to La Liga with Valencia.

9 - David Luiz

A polarising figure following his 2019 arrival from Chelsea, his two seasons were a rollercoaster of costly red cards and moments of brilliance. Despite the chaotic moments, his leadership off the pitch was vital during Arsenal's 2020 FA Cup triumph.

View 7 Images Luiz's arrival raised some eyebrows (Image: Getty)

‌



8 - Denilson

Signed from Sao Paulo as a teenager in 2006, the midfielder went on to clock up over 150 appearances during a transitional period for Wenger's side. While often scrutinised for his side-ways passing style, he proved to be a somewhat dependable option over five years in an inexperienced squad.

7 - Julio Baptista

'The Beast' spent the 2006/07 season on loan from Real Madrid as part of the exchange deal for Jose Antonio Reyes. Though inconsistent in the Premier League, his legendary four-goal demolition of Liverpool at Anfield in the League Cup etched his name in Arsenal lore. He netted a not-terrible 10 goals in 35 appearances before returning to Los Blancos.

View 7 Images Baptista didn't exactly thrive in north London (Image: Getty)

‌



6 - Sylvinho

Wenger's first-ever Brazilian recruit arrived in 1999 and quickly became a fan favourite thanks to his energetic runs and stunning long-range strikes. He racked up 80 appearances before passport complications unfortunately cut his Highbury career short in 2001, allowing a young Ashley Cole to take over at left-back.

5 - Gabriel Jesus

He arrived from Manchester City in 2022 and instantly revitalised Arsenal's attack. Unfortunately, the striker's career in N5 took a turn for the worse in late 2022 after his injury at the World Cup with Brazil. Since then, he has constantly battled niggles and a serious ACL injury, losing his spark but still managing to lift the Premier League trophy last season.

4 - Gabriel Martinelli

Plucked from the Brazilian lower leagues as an unknown teenager in 2019, he developed into one of the Premier League's best left wingers under Arteta. His progress has somewhat halted in recent seasons but his relentless work ethic and clutch goals have made him a crucial pillar of Arsenal's title-chasing era.

‌



View 7 Images Jesus, Martinelli and Gabriel are Premier League champions (Image: Getty )

3 - Edu Gaspar

A reliable midfielder who earned legendary status as a member of the iconic 2003/04 'Invincibles', winning two Premier League titles and two FA Cups during Wenger's tenure. He later returned to shape the club's modern era as sporting director, driving Arsenal's resurgence before departing in late 2024.

2 - Gabriel Magalhaes

Signed from Lille in 2020, the imposing centre-back has developed into a defensive cornerstone and a massive threat from set-pieces. Forming an elite partnership with William Saliba, he has established himself as one of the best defenders in Europe, with the potential to become Arsenal's greatest ever Brazilian by the time he hangs up his boots.

‌



1 - Gilberto Silva

View 7 Images Gilberto is Arsenal's greatest Brazilian (Image: Getty)

'The Invisible Wall' was the serene anchor of the undefeated 2003/04 Invincibles and scored the club's first competitive goal at the Emirates Stadium.

A World Cup winner and a true Arsenal legend, he brought invaluable composure and defensive bite across 244 appearances for the club.

Liverpool news: Andoni Iraola eyes £188m raid as gloomy prediction made by Reds hero

Liverpool believed to be looking to pull off a mega move in the transfer market this summer

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola is eyeing a major transfer raid (Image: Getty Images)

After a quiet summer, Liverpool could be set to significantly step up their transfer activity. The clock is ticking with the Reds set to face Newcastle in their opening game of the new Premier League on Sunday, August 23.

Sports.content:

Sports.title: Joe Ward: The unluckiest man in Irish boxing
Sports.content:
Joe Ward had the world at his feet. He was an amateur boxing sensation, he had a golden future laid out before him. Until disaster struck, over and over again.

In 2011 Ward made history, becoming the youngest Irish boxer to win a gold medal at the senior European Championships.

Even at that early stage hype was building for what Ward could accomplish at the London Olympics. But at the 2012 qualification event, tucked away in Trabzon in Turkey, the teenage Ward lost a contentious decision to the host nation boxer.

"My main goal was always to get to the Olympics in London. Trabzon just wasn't to be, as you know. It felt like we won the fight and we just didn't get the decision," Ward told Sky Sports.

He regrouped and made the 2016 Olympics his target. He reached the Rio Games, only to crash out at the first stage as the referee gave him two baffling points deductions, tipping the three-round amateur bout in his opponent's favour.

"It was one of these things that was out of my control," Ward reflected. "I picked up two public warnings, where I was still winning on the scorecards but because of the warnings I was beaten on a 3-2 split decision. Definitely at that time I was very disheartened.

"I was kind of saying to myself: 'Am I ever going to get that little bit of luck?' But again after a few weeks you just regroup and go back to the gym."

Image: Ward was a superstar of Irish amateur boxing

He won three European golds in all and a cluster of World Championship medals.

"It's not an accident to be consistently winning," he said. "You have to have something a little bit special about you. I believe so."

But an Olympic medal could have taken put him on a completely different trajectory. That was something he was denied.

"I kind of always focus on the future," he reflected. "Sometimes you can overthink about what's gone. It's not going to change anything.

"I've always loved boxing and loved being around it and it's something that gave me huge opportunities in my life, to travel the world and meet so many great people. For me I just don't think there's anything else.

"It's something that I love doing."

Eventually, in 2019, he turned professional. He had his first pro fight at Madison Square Garden in New York, it was all set up for him. Then painful disaster struck.

In the second round his knee dislocated and collapsed beneath him. His debut could scarcely have been gone worse.

"You kind of question it sometimes," Ward said. "It could have happened somewhere else but I believe everything happens for a reason. It was out of my control. It was one of these freak accidents that happen. Obviously it was devastating when it happened, I was very upset.

"Mentally you don't want to leave the game, you always want to be involved. Sometimes injuries can stop that from happening, I was hoping that that my knee wasn't going to stop me continuing chasing my goals and my career. It was good that everything worked out well with the operation and they said there were no more issues."

The business of boxing can be unforgiving. Opportunities dried up, but Ward stayed patient, fought on and now on Saturday, live on Sky Sports, he takes on hard-punching, undefeated light-heavyweight contender Artjom Kasparian in Dublin.

Image: Ward fights Artjom Kasparian on Saturday live on Sky Sports

"There's no point getting in there to take easy fights," he said. "It's an opportunity to step up and fight decent fighters and move on and challenge myself to see how far I can really take it. I really believe in myself, I can go all the way.

"That's the key, just getting the opportunity, getting the right fights at the right time. It felt like that never happened over the last couple of years."

He believes all that misfortune, the bad luck that has shrouded his talent, will now help him.

"Things will change, you will get a bit of luck along the way," Ward said. "That makes you a stronger person. I feel like that will give you the extra edge then when something happens in a fight or a moment where you just need something different. That will always flash back - look, I've been through it all and now I can fight through this.

"The most important thing as a fighter is to still believe in yourself, still stay focused, still keep in the gym, keep learning. Doors will open for you, opportunities will come.

"I've had a lot of ups and downs in my career but looking back I'm grateful for opportunities and grateful for what I've achieved. I just stuck at it and here I am still going strong, still believe in myself, believe I'm probably the best I've ever been physically, mentally. So I'm excited."

Sports.title: Rockets march on after easy win while Buttler makes history in The Hundred
Sports.content:
Trent Rockets extended their lead at the top of The Hundred table with a near-perfect performance that secured their fifth win in six games, leaving Birmingham Phoenix rooted to the bottom.

Sam Billings' unbeaten 31 sealed a scrappy chase after Phoenix stuttered to 111-6 despite Joe Clarke's 50, while Jos Buttler made history for the Manchester Super Giants as he became the leading Twenty20 run-scorer of all time.

After the Rockets elected to field, Will Smeed broke an unwanted record by being the first batter in The Hundred history to be unbeaten without scoring at the end of the powerplay. 25 runs came from that powerplay for the loss of Mitch Owen to Mohammad Amir, who had to leave the field with a strained hamstring immediately after taking the wicket.

Smeed eventually fell for six off 16 balls, with the visitors appearing tentative against a disciplined attack led by outstanding performances from spinners Calvin Harrison and Mitch Santner, along with Lewis Gregory.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A crowd member made a great catch during Trent Rockets match against Birmingham Phoenix

Only Joe Clarke, Phoenix's leading run-scorer this season, managed to break free, reaching a half-century from 37 balls before finishing with 62 off 47. He became the fourth victim of Craig Overton's safe hands, with the catches setting a competition record. Of the remaining batters, only Laurie Evans reached double figures as Phoenix limped to an underwhelming 111-6 from their 100 balls.

After Amir's departure, skipper Billings had juggled his bowlers expertly as he searches for a fourth successive title in The Hundred. And when the Rockets batted, there was little pressure on the openers, Ben Duckett and Finn Allen progressing smoothly to 29-0 in the powerplay.

Mystery spinner Usman Tariq removed Duckett for 22 and delivered his customary bow celebration, conceding just six runs from his first 10 balls. However, there were simply not enough runs on the board, with 113 becoming the lowest total ever successfully defended in The Hundred men's competition.

Nye Donald came and went after a typically pugnacious six-ball 17, before Allen and Billings calmly rotated the strike at around a run a ball. Two successive sixes from Billings off Saqib Mahmood, including an outrageous slog sweep, accelerated the finish, and the result was all but confirmed when Allen holed out to Tariq at short mid-on for 28 with only six runs required.

The Rockets completed the victory with another Billings six, winning with 17 balls to spare to be sitting pretty with two games to come, their route direct to the final having got that bit easier.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Overton makes FOUR great catches for Trent Rockets

Gregory said: "We were superb with the ball. We kept chipping away with important wickets. It was a little bit two-paced, with a bit of variable bounce at times. The bowling unit spoke about smashing the top of the stump as hard as we could.

"The guys up front with the bat have been outstanding. We're in a really good position, playing some fantastic cricket, and hopefully we can continue that."

Buttler become the leading Twenty20 run-scorer of all time

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jos Buttler hits a mega half century to win it for Manchester Super Giants vs Welsh Fire

After three straight defeats, Manchester Super Giants got the win they needed over Welsh Fire at an overcast Emirates Old Trafford to remain in contention for qualification.

Half-centuries from Tim Seifert and Jos Buttler propelling them to a crunching win with 31 balls to spare.

Seifert said: "We just tried to get off to a good start and maintain the run rate and it was good that we both got going. And it was quite nice to watch Buttler from the other end! We've got two big games ahead and this is a good little boost for us."

The Super Giants move up to 12 points, now just four behind the Fire with two games left each.

They had to do it without their captain Aiden Markram, who has returned to South Africa for personal reasons, Jos Buttler taking over captaincy duties and Paul Walter replacing him at the top of the order, meaning there were just three overseas players in the line-up.

Second-placed Fire won the toss and chose to bat, reaching an uncomfortable 4-0 from the first ten balls after Josh Tongue didn't concede a single run off his first five balls.

Short was particularly severe on Noor Ahmad, who conceded 34 runs from 15 balls, while Sonny Baker was even more expensive. He celebrated the milestone by clearing the ropes in each of the next two balls, before adding further successive sixes to bring up a 20-ball half-century and guide his side home with ease.

Sports.title: Infantino remains FIFA president following crisis meeting
Sports.content:
Under-fire FIFA president Gianni Infantino has shaken off calls to resign - for now - with the backing of the governing body's leaders, though apologised for "mistakes" in his botched attempts to sell off a stake in the World Cup.

In a statement released after seven hours of crisis talks in Morocco, FIFA said its management board had re-affirmed their "full support" for Infantino - including secretary general Mattias Grafstrom, only days after he had labelled the World Cup plans "a sad and reproachable series of events". The pair were later seen laughing together watching a Women's AFCON game in Rabat.

Infantino had faced mounting calls to resign following the leak of previously undiscussed proposals, after it was revealed national associations had not been consulted and had been given a deadline barely a month away in mid-September and the promise of a £30.1m incentive to back them.

In a letter seen by Sky News sent to national associations and signed by Infantino and Grafstrom, the pair wrote that they "sincerely apologised for the errors" in the plans which were eventually withdrawn on Saturday following days of criticism from across world football.

A second statement released publicly through FIFA.com hit back at those critics, threatening that FIFA would "no longer tolerate any attacks on its integrity, good governance and due process and will take all necessary measures to protect and safeguard its name and reputation".

FIFA said it had "not been the intention… for member associations to feel excluded from the process" and admitted they should have been "handled differently" while further acknowledging "errors were also made after the proposal was leaked to media."

The governing body also promised a review would be conducted into the fiasco and a report into its findings presented at the next FIFA Council, comprising 37 national representatives from around world football.

Infantino and FIFA's reputation had taken increasing hits from inside and outside of its own walls over the plans with Arsene Wenger, its chief of global football development, distancing himself publicly while Infantino's personal senior advisor Carlos Cordeiro quit his role on Friday, labelling them a "bad deal" and "irresponsible".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports’ Kaveh Solhekol explains whether Gianni Infantino will walk away from FIFA after crisis meeting

The head of the Jordan FA went further by accusing Infantino of "blackmail", while UEFA announced it had "lost confidence in the current FIFA leadership" and the FA called for a "full and robust review of FIFA's leadership".

Those calls had grown further on Wednesday as legendary winger Luis Figo labelled Infantino's actions "the lowest, most deceitful and cravenly self-interested behaviour I have ever witnessed" while Canada prime minister Mark Carney - whose country had welcomed Infantino in as World Cup co-hosts only weeks earlier - said the incident should be "fatal" for his position as FIFA president.

FIFA did not address those calls directly and instead said the marathon meeting would "strengthen FIFA's governance, help restore confidence in the organisation and enable us to prepare for the major events and challenges ahead in a united and transparent manner".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney speaks out on his lack of confidence in FIFA president Gianni Infantino following his private investment plans.

What next for Infantino? 'Associations have levers to force him out'

Sky Sports News' chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol:

Infantino is a man with a very thick skin, obviously he's aware of what is being said about him - but his feeling all along has been that he was elected president by the 211 associations around the world which make up FIFA and if he's going to be removed, it's going to be by them.

The Prime Minister of Canada, Mark Carney, said he's lost confidence in Infantino. That's significant because Canada were one of the three co-hosts at the World Cup this summer, and Carney was at the World Cup final two and a half weeks ago sat near Infantino.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol provides the latest update regarding the ongoing situation with Infantino, as the Football Association is set to withdraw their support for the FIFA president

I don't think him refusing to resign is something all the associations around the world are going to accept after losing faith in him. They have a few other levers they can use to try to force him out.

There could be an emergency FIFA Council with a vote of no confidence, and he would be out if he lost. There could be an emergency FIFA Congress, with the same outcome.

If he wants to cling on and wait until the next presidential election in March, he may feel he has the numbers to get re-elected despite the opposition against him.

The date to look out for in that case is November 18, the deadline for candidates to declare themselves.

He has got his calculator out and still feels he has support in different parts of the world - South America, Africa and parts of Asia. He feels he lives to fight another day.

What were FIFA's World Cup plans?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Martyn Ziegler joins the Paper Talk team to discuss Infantino's future at FIFA

Under the initial proposal to launch FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), football's world governing body aimed to raise up to $4.2bn (£3.1bn) from external investors through the sale of minority, non-controlling stakes in FFE, which it said would be valued at around $20bn (£15bn).

The governing body said its plans - which would have required approval from member associations - could deliver more than $10bn in "football development funding" over the next four years.

Who could replace Infantino?

Sky Sports News' chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol:

There's been talk about the president of Paris Saint-Germain, Nasser Al-Khelaifi, one of the most powerful men in world football, who is on the UEFA executive committee. But my understanding is that he is not interested in replacing Infantino.

Other candidates are people like Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, who came second in the vote to become FIFA president 10 years ago. He's the president of the AFC, who also oppose the sell-off plans.

Then there's the president of CONCACAF, Victor Montagliani. We've just had the World Cup in three CONCACAF countries and historically, CONCACAF have been close to Infantino, but they said on Thursday that they rejected the proposal as well.

Finally, someone I think would be very popular is Aleksander Ceferin, the president of UEFA. He has a totally different vision about the way football should be run. If he was the president of FIFA, there would be no hydration breaks, no FIFA Peace Prizes, no Qatari-owned private jets for the president, no $1m (£742,000) World Cup tickets.

But I don't think Ceferin has ever expressed any desire or interest publicly to replace Infantino.

Perhaps we are getting ahead of ourselves. Infantino is under a lot of pressure and it would be fair to say he is fighting for his job, but we are not at the stage where people are going to come out and say they are going to stand against him.

Sports.title: Castleford head coach Carr to miss the game against Hull KR
Sports.content:
Castleford Tigers head coach Ryan Carr will not be in attendance at the Hull KR game due to personal reasons.

Chris Chester, Scott Murrell and Rob Nickolay will lead the team in his absence and they will be supported by club legend and Man of Steel Adrian Vowles.

Australian Carr took charge in pre-season on a three-year deal having previously been coach of Featherstone Rovers and assistant manager at Leeds Rhinos in 2019.

A statement released by the club read: "Castleford Tigers RLFC can confirm that head coach Ryan Carr will not be in attendance at the Hull KR game this coming Friday. We can confirm that this is due to personal reasons, contrary to the reports on social media.

"In the interim, Chris Chester, Rob Nickolay and Scott Murrell will lead our on and off field operations. This leadership group will be heavily supported by Adrian Vowles and we thank Adrian for offering his support at short notice.

"We will not be making any other further comment at this stage, and we urge our fans to once again get behind our team this coming Friday."

Castleford currently sit ninth in the Super League table with seven wins from 21 games.

With six games remaining in the season, they face the Robins followed by Hull FC, St Helens, Catalans Dragons, Bradford Bulls, and Huddersfield Giants.

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+.

Sports.title: Arsenal players 'fuming' after defeat to Real Betis in Dublin friendly
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta revealed his players were "fuming" after Arsenal produced a sloppy performance as they were beaten 3-1 by LaLiga side Real Betis in a pre-season friendly in Dublin.

The Gunners fell behind when Kepa Arrizabalaga came out and failed to claim a corner, allowing Rodrigo Riquelme to score at the back post. Nelson Deossa added a stunning second from long range.

Arsenal pulled one back when an inswinging corner from new signing Christos Tzolis was headed over the line by Piero Hincapie but Betis restored their two-goal lead when Pablo Fornals found the bottom corner following a misplaced pass by Kai Havertz.

How did Arsenal line up? Starting XI: Kepa, White, Mosquera, Hincapie, Calafiori, Lewis-Skelly, Havertz, Nwaneri, Dowman, Gyokeres, Tzolis



Subbed on: Copley, Salmon, Gabriel, Vieira, Nelson, Jesus, Martinelli, Julienne, Meslier, Ibrahim, Ogunnaike, Clarke, Kabia, O'Neill

Mikel Arteta made second-half changes with Brazil internationals Gabriel and Gabriel Martinelli given their first cameos of pre-season but Arsenal, still without Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard and others involved at the World Cup, were unable to cut the deficit.

When asked about the mood in the dressing room after defeat, Arteta revealed: "Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That's what we need."

The defeat, their first of pre-season, comes as Arsenal continue to push for new signings in the transfer market, with the club having agreed a £75m fee with Newcastle for Bruno Guimaraes.

The key moments from Dublin

9 - GOAL! Kepa Arrizabalaga fails to claim a corner, allowing the unmarked Rodrigo Riquelme to score at the far post

Kepa Arrizabalaga fails to claim a corner, allowing the unmarked Rodrigo Riquelme to score at the far post 26 - GOAL! Nelson Deossa adds Real Betis's stunning second goal with a powerful long-range effort

Nelson Deossa adds Real Betis's stunning second goal with a powerful long-range effort 32 - GOAL! Christos Tzolis's inswinging corner loops over the Real Betis goalkeeper and is headed in by Piero Hincapie

Christos Tzolis's inswinging corner loops over the Real Betis goalkeeper and is headed in by Piero Hincapie 43 - GOAL! Pablo Fornals fires home a third goal for Real Betis following a misplaced pass by Kai Havertz

Pablo Fornals fires home a third goal for Real Betis following a misplaced pass by Kai Havertz 46 - SUBS! Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta makes seven half-time changes, with returning Brazilians Gabriel and Gabriel Martinelli among those introduced

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta makes seven half-time changes, with returning Brazilians Gabriel and Gabriel Martinelli among those introduced 55 - INJURY! Arsenal youngster Louie Copley is forced off with a serious-looking knee injury

Arsenal youngster Louie Copley is forced off with a serious-looking knee injury 64 - SAVE! Real Betis cut through Arsenal but Illan Meslier saves Isco's close-range flick

Real Betis cut through Arsenal but Illan Meslier saves Isco's close-range flick 67 - SHOT! Martinelli tees up a chance for Gabriel Jesus, who fires wide

Did Arsenal show need for Bruno?

With a lengthy list of players still to return following the World Cup, Arteta gave another chance to the midfield trio of Myles Lewis-Skelly, Ethan Nwaneri and Kai Havertz following the victory over Girona. This time, they found it more difficult.

Lewis-Skelly had some bright moments on the ball at No 6. He completed 70 of his 74 passes. But he couldn't provide the same level of defensive coverage of Rice, Martin Zubimendi, or indeed Guimaraes, whose move from Newcastle is getting closer.

Lewis-Skelly should still have a significant role to play for Arsenal this season. But Arsenal's struggles in midfield in Dublin showed why the club have pursued Guimaraes so aggressively. He will add elite quality and give Arsenal a level of depth their midfield currently lacks.

Of course, pre-season results count for little. This was primarily a fitness-building exercise for Arsenal. But their uncharacteristic openness leaves Arteta with food for thought right across the pitch as the Premier League champions prepare to defend their crown.

Image: Riccardo Calafiori challenges for the ball against Real Betis

Arteta: We didn't compete to our standards

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta to Premier Sports:

"Always upset when you lose a football match.

"Two very different halves, especially with the personnel we played today.

"The first half, we wanted two different things - play well and compete well. We did the first one quite well in a lot of moments. But the compete part, especially in and around our box, was not at our standards to win a football match against a good side.

"We have to have dominance. The first goal, the action from the corner, we concede a sloppy goal. Then we gave two giveaways very close to our box as well. They were very efficient, two very good goals as well from their side.

"It's always good when you lose a match in pre-season; it creates a bit more fire in the belly.

"It's better to give those goals away in a friendly match than an official match.

"It's a balance between understanding where we are and the personnel we are playing - and the demands that are at the highest level."

Sports.title: Pakistan end eight-match away Test losing streak ahead of England clash
Sports.content:
Pakistan ended their eight-match away Test losing streak in emphatic fashion on Wednesday, securing an eight-wicket victory over the West Indies.

First innings century-maker Abdullah Shafique and Babar Azam, in his first series since being reappointed as captain, led Pakistan to 77-2 with unbeaten knocks of 24 runs each as the visitors achieved victory shortly after lunch on day four and draw the series at 1-1.

Babar knocked off the target by hitting back-to-back sixes against left-arm spinner Jomel Warrican, whose six-wicket haul in the first innings had limited Pakistan's lead to 43 runs.

"You are always satisfied with the win," Babar said. "The most important thing was that we executed our plans whether it was how Abdullah Shafique batting or how the spinners bowled in the second innings."

Babar's decision to leave out his in-form fast bowler Mohammad Abbas in favour of extra spinner was vindicated as West Indies' batting crumbled against Pakistan's slow bowlers in the second innings.

"When we saw the pitch it looked more similar to how they are in Pakistan," Babar said. "We decided to play an additional spinner and it had an impact on our combinations because of which we had to leave out our senior players."

West Indies won the first Test by 90 runs in Tarouba, but Pakistan's spinners Sajid Khan and Ali Usman capitalised on favourable conditions on a wearing Queen's Park Oval pitch to help their side remain unbeaten in a Test series against West Indies since 2000.

Pakistan lost the wickets of Imam-ul-Haq, brilliantly snapped up by Justin Greaves in the slips cordon for nine in Jayden Seales' first over, and Azan Awais was bowled by Shamar Joseph for 18 before Shafique and Babar sealed the win inside four days.

Masood was eventually relieved of the captaincy after Pakistan's struggles in red-ball cricket, but Babar's return as skipper brought no immediate turnaround, with the Tarouba defeat marking Pakistan's eighth away Test loss in three years.
