Sports.title: Kepa could LOSE his place as No 2 after another error, Arsenal's glaring frailty is exposed and forgotten star shows why he can have a future at the club: THINGS WE LEARNED as Gunners are beaten by Real Betis
Sports.content:
Arsenal were comfortably beaten 3-1 by Real Betis in Dublin in their second pre-season match following a string of errors in the first-half.

Kepa Arrizabalaga's poor display brought his place in the squad into question, before a number of changes in the second-half slowed things down.

The Gunners will take on Borussia Dortmund and Como in the rest of pre-season before the Community Shield, and then their Premier League title defence will kick off at home to Coventry.

Daily Mail Sport's ISAAN KHAN was at the Aviva Stadium to run the rule over the game.

Kepa could lose spot

The signing of Illan Meslier as Arsenal's third choice goalkeeper took most by surprise.

With the established Arrizabalaga as No 2, a potential pathway didn't seem clear for Meslier.

Arsenal were beaten 3-1 by LaLiga side Real Betis in their latest pre-season outing in Ireland

Kepa Arrizabalaga was at fault for at least one of the goals and could lose his place as No 2

Though the reasons for the Frenchman's signing looked clear as day on the basis of this display against Real Betis.

For the Spanish team's first goal on nine minutes, Kepa aimlessly charged out, flapping at Pablo Garcia's corner kick and completely missing it.

It landed to Rodrigo Riquelme at the back post, who chested the ball down and struck it home.

The second goal he conceded, a stunning long-range strike from Nelson Deossa, was not an error. But the lead up was, his poor clearance eventually finding Deossa to score.

The Spaniard was beaten by another impressive shot from outside the area just before half-time, Pablo Fornals making the score 3-1 after Piero Hincapie's headed goal.

This match isn't an isolated example, either. Take the Carabao Cup final against Manchester City in March, where a Kepa howler paved the way to Arsenal's defeat.

At the level Arsenal are at, hunting for silverware across a myriad of competitions next season, they can ill-afford an error-prone No 2.

Mikel Arteta has shown his ruthlessness with goalkeepers before, as seen by the Aaron Ramsdale and David Raya saga, Ramsdale eventually sold on.

Selling Kepa would not be controversial and make sense if a plausible offer came in.

Tommy Setford, 20, was third-choice keeper last season and could do the same job this time round.

A confused Gunners defence shipped two goals and frailties opened up at the back

A confused defence

Pre-season friendlies may not officially count, though certain frailties can emerge.

A glaring one reared its head in Dublin – a confused defence, unsure whether to commit or stand off.

For two of Betis' goals, the backline's decision to drop off allowed Deossa and Fornals' shots to sail in from distance.

The lack of cohesion was improved in the second period with the introduction of Gabriel.

The wider gap stands, though – without William Saliba, Arsenal's defence is noticeably weaker.

Piero Hincapie looked particularly lost in positioning, the left back accustomed to a different slot.

It is hard to switch between the two positions, in fairness, with both roles rather different.

Still, it reflects just why Arsenal are keen to bring in a centre back this summer.

It's an area that needs bolstering in a squad hunting for trophies across a myriad of competitions next season.

A role for Nwaneri?

There is some player in Ethan Nwaneri – which is why Arsenal haven't let him go thus far.

The magic he holds in his boots is clear. He danced away, evading players to effortlessly place through balls to his team-mates.

The Betis backline retreated, Nwaneri making it clear his willingness to proceed in one direction: forward.

Early on, the teenager put a tackle in and wriggled away to get his team forward.

Later, there were other forays which put the opposition on alert. His tight dribbling skill at pace is hard to contain when the forward is on song.

Though, the context must be remembered, the 19-year-old's career having frozen somewhat. He was loaned to Marseille in January this year under Roberto de Zerbi, who rated the teenager.

Though once De Zerbi was sacked the following month, with Habib Beye shunting Nwaneri to the bench.

He is now taking his opportunities and leaves Arteta with a conundrum for the weeks ahead.

Ethan Nwaneri is now taking his opportunities and Mikel Arteta must now make a decision on his future

The forward line

The battle for Arsenal's No 9 slot is up for grabs.

Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz barely played together last season because of Havertz's knee issues.

Arteta's preference last season was the German as the main No9 with Gyokeres complementing him, before the enforced change transpired.

It remains to be seen how Arteta goes about this conundrum for the next campaign.

On two minutes, Havertz charged into the area and squared the ball to Gyokeres who dithered, his shot saved by Alvaro Valles.

The Swede ought to have done better and didn't make an impression in his display.

Havertz didn't pull up trees, either, but has now started consecutive matches which is promising after his previous fitness record.

Both players have a battle on their hands to seize the top spot.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher questions Mo Salah's Trabzonspor move as he claims star is too good for Turkey - as ex-Liverpool man breaks silence on surprise switch and THOUSANDS gather to greet him
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher questions Mo Salah's Trabzonspor move as he claims star is too good for Turkey - as ex-Liverpool man breaks silence on surprise switch and THOUSANDS gather to greet him

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Mo Salah is 'better than Turkey' and could have moved to more prestigious clubs than Trabzonspor, claims Jamie Carragher.

On Wednesday, Salah was given an extraordinary reception by 25,000 jubilant fans at Trabzon airport ahead of putting pen to paper on a two-year deal.

Supporters let off flares and rolled out the red carpet for the most high-profile addition in club history.

The Liverpool legend, who left the Reds this summer a year into his two-year contract extension, had been deliberating for some time over his next destination.

Carragher felt Salah might want to keep testing himself at the highest level he could, in one of Europe's top leagues.

He told the Football Ramble: 'I never believed he was going to go to Saudi, because number one, he's too good for that. I think he can be playing in Serie A. Turkey for me feels a level too low.

Thousands of Trabzonspor supporters gathered to greet Mo Salah after he landed

There were extraordinary scenes to welcome the biggest signing in Trabzonspor history

O bize, biz ona hayran 🤷‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/8Q3GCHu1C6 — Trabzonspor (@Trabzonspor) August 5, 2026

'I was convinced he'd end up at an AC Milan or Juventus or somewhere like that, maybe his wages were a problem. Looking at him, I don't know him, obviously have never spoken to him.

'But he's like Ronaldo, he's so driven, his numbers mean so much to him. I thought, he can still do this in Turkey by the way, but I thought he'd want to play at a real prestigious club.

He went on: 'Obviously his wage demands have put a few people off but I thought he might almost curb those demands a little bit to almost get a better club.

'To go to an AC Milan or Juventus or whoever it may be, play at the San Siro, still playing in big games, still playing in Europe. Turkey just feels like... I just think he's better than that.'

Salah was given an extraordinary welcome by Trabzonspor fans, with tens of thousands greeting him at Trabzon airport.

The Egyptian wore a broad smile and lapped up the acclaim as flares were set off and supporters celebrated into the night.

Salah was adorned in Trabzonspor gear and wore a scarf around his neck as he addressed the crowds.

He said: 'I honestly can't even remember if I've seen something like this before. I'm very happy to be here. There are 25,000 fans, it's UNBELIEVABLE!'

Is Turkey a level too low for Mo Salah?



Jamie Carragher reveals where he thinks the Egyptian winger should've gone instead.



To hear more of our chat with Jamie on yesterday's pod, listen here! 👉 https://t.co/iRus940XLd pic.twitter.com/Zit4MqgTnM — Football Ramble (@FootballRamble) August 5, 2026

'I'm incredibly happy to be in this incredible atmosphere. Have I seen something like this before... I honestly can't remember. Seeing this kind of love and attention makes me so happy.'

'I'll work very hard to achieve success in the league and in Europe. Because I've won successes at every club I've joined. I've always been a successful footballer. And that's what I'll do here too.'

Earlier on Wednesday, Salah was pictured on a jet ahead of his impending signing wearing a Trabzonspor shirt, featuring his name and the number 61 - which is regularly used as a symbol of the city and the club.

Trabzonspor had invited their supporters to pay to join a live stream following Salah's flight to Turkey, as fans gathered outside the Ataturk Airport ahead of his arrival.

A private jet took off from Mykonos Airport around 10.30am as Salah began his journey.

Turkish giants Besiktas were understood to be the Egyptian's first choice but talks with them stalled last week.

Trabzonspor revealed their talks with Salah on Tuesday night, with the club informing their 1.9million followers on X of his travel arrangements, as well as telling fans a welcome programme would be in place.

Salah's future has been the subject of huge interest since the surprising decision was announced back in March that he would leave Liverpool one year into his two-year contract extension.

It was pandemonium in the Turkish city after the club announced the travel details of Salah

The Turkish side rolled out the red carpet for the former Liverpool winger

Many anticipated that Saudi Arabia would be the most likely destination after Al-Ittihad made a £150million bid in summer 2023.

But Trabzonspor are now set to sign the winger, who fell out with Arne Slot at Anfield last term.

The Turkish side finished third last season behind Fenerbahce and champions Galatasaray.

Salah, who is the third-highest goalscorer in Reds history with 255, did not engage in talks with teams before the end of the season out of respect to the Merseyside club.

Salah will be the most high-profile signing in Trabzonspor's history and when his move is confirmed, will join Man United loanee Andre Onana.

Ex-Man City defender Stefan Savic also plays for the Turkish side, who have won their domestic title seven times.

Sports.title: Real Madrid confident of seeing off Arsenal interest in Vinicius Jr after offering improved £19m deal - as Brazilian adds to uncertainty by deleting entire Instagram history
Sports.content:
Real Madrid are awaiting a response from Vinicius Jr after offering the Arsenal target improved terms in excess of £19million a year.

The Brazil international’s current terms with Madrid expire at the end of next season and Arsenal have made him aware they are willing to step in if he fails to find agreement with the Spanish giants.

Talks between the player’s agents, general director Jose Angel Sanchez and chief scout Juni Calafat took place in Madrid on Wednesday. Jose Mourinho also underlined that the 26-year-old is also firmly in his plans.

Real are believed to be increasingly confident of keeping the Brazilian superstar Vinicius Jr at the Bernabeu.

Despite the increased confidence at the Bernabeu, the player added to the uncertainty on Wednesday night by deleting his entire Instagram history.

Vinicius' page, which has 63.9million followers, currently displays no images or bio and he's also removed his profile picture.

Vinicius Junior in training with Real Madrid this week as the transfer saga takes another twist

Vinicius Jr deleted all the content from his Instagram, which was mostly Real Madrid related

The dramatic move - not uncommon among footballers - could be interpreted in a number of different ways but typically can be interpreted as dissatisfaction with the current club.

All of the Real Madrid training and playing images that featured prominently on his account have now gone.

Waiting in the wings and hoping to capitalise on the situation are Arsenal.

The Gunners made initial enquiries into the player last week, with manager Mikel Arteta insisting that the Premier League winners will be 'very ambitious' during the summer's transfer window.

But reports on Wednesday suggested Madrid were bullish about their chances of seeing off interest from north London - particularly with Mourinho's backing.

One of the major sticking points in negotiations between Real and Vinicius' camp has been the re-signing fee.

But the latest increase in their offer has left Real confident that Vinicius Jr will commit his future to the Spanish giants.

Real do not want to lose the Brazilian on a free, with his contract set to expire in less than a year.

The player is thought to view any contract he signs with Los Blancos, where he has played since 2018, as the defining deal of his career - and recognition of his efforts for the club that in recent seasons have seen him become a Ballon d'Or contender in their colours.

Vinicius returned to join his team-mates at their pre-season camp on Monday to undergo the standard start-of-season medical tests and train for the first time under new manager Mourinho.

Arteta meanwhile has remained upbeat about his plans for the rest of the window, following the £34m signing of Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge.

‘We expect to have movements in the next few weeks, obviously,’ Arteta said following Arsenal's pre-season friendly against Girona.

‘We want to get better like anybody else, and you can see the transfer market and our opponents... We won't sit still and we are very ambitious with what we are doing.

‘The margins are very small. Because we want to get better and the level is going to increase.

'We need to increase the competition internally. We need to make sure we identify the things that we don't have in the team.’

Sports.title: Matthias Jaissle insists Newcastle have a 'clear vision' for the future after being confirmed Eddie Howe's successor - despite summer upheaval as captain Bruno Guimaraes nears Arsenal move
Sports.content:
Matthias Jaissle insists Newcastle have a 'clear vision' for the future after being confirmed Eddie Howe's successor - despite summer upheaval as captain Bruno Guimaraes nears Arsenal move

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Matthias Jaissle has declared he believes 'unreservedly' in Newcastle's ambition and direction for the future after being confirmed as Eddie Howe's successor.

The German coach joins from Saudi Arabian side Al-Ahli, where he led the PIF-owned club to Asian Champions League success in 2025 and 2026.

Jaissle's appointment comes amid a summer of upheaval at Newcastle, with Howe's five-year spell in charge coming to an end along with the departures of several star names.

Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali left earlier in the summer for Barcelona and Tottenham, while club captain Bruno Guimaraes is closing in on a £75million move to Arsenal.

Jaissle, 38, stressed that Newcastle have a 'clear vision' as he vowed to work to deliver success to the club.

'It is an incredible honour to become head coach of Newcastle United. This is one of the biggest clubs in European football, with a unique history, identity and supporter base, and I am excited to experience that passion and connection first-hand,' Jaissle said.

Matthias Jaissle has been confirmed as Newcastle's new head coach after Eddie Howe's exit

Jaissle takes over amid a summer of upheaval at Newcastle, with captain Bruno Guimaraes set to follow Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali in leaving the club

'When Newcastle United comes your way, you take notice. The ambition of the club, the vision for the future and the opportunity ahead made this an incredibly compelling place to be. I have followed the club's journey closely in recent years and the progress that has been made is clear for everyone to see.

'I am incredibly excited about the future. I fully and unreservedly believe in this project, the ambition and the direction the club is taking. There is a clear vision, strong leadership and an exceptional platform to build on.

'My teams are built on togetherness, hard work, intensity and a passion to improve every single day. I will bring full commitment, full energy and a determination to give everything I have to help this club achieve its ambitions.

'I believe there is enormous potential within this squad and throughout the football club. I am excited to work with the players, staff and leadership team to help take the club forward.

'I cannot wait to get started and will attack this opportunity. I give my complete commitment and total energy to bringing further success to Newcastle United.'

Jaissle will take charge for the first time when Newcastle face Valencia on Saturday at the end of the camp in La Manga.

Newcastle have described Jaissle as 'one of Europe's leading young coaches', with the club stating that he emerged as the 'clear outstanding candidate' during their recruitment process.

Jaissle had previously coached Red Bull Salzburg and led the club to two Austrian titles, before moving to Al-Ahli, where he guided the Saudi Arabian side to successive AFC Champions League triumphs.

We’re delighted to announce the appointment of Matthias Jaissle as Newcastle United head coach. ✍️



Welcome to the club, Matthias! 🖤🤍 pic.twitter.com/C1kNstwg8X — Newcastle United (@NUFC) August 5, 2026

Howe confirmed he was stepping down as Newcastle boss in a statement last week

Howe led Newcastle to their first major trophy in 70 years in 2025 and also took them to the Champions League on two occasions

'Matthias' leadership style and football philosophy are strongly aligned with our sporting vision,' said Ross Wilson, Newcastle's sporting director.

'His teams play high-energy football and we could feel his passion during all of our discussions throughout the recruitment process.

'He has consistently demonstrated an ability to improve players, build cohesive teams and create elite performance environments in his coaching career.

'His successes at Salzburg and Al-Ahli underline his ability to deliver results while developing a clear football identity.

'We believe he is uniquely positioned to build on the strong foundations already in place and help take Newcastle United forward.'

After a steady start to the summer, the final month of the transfer window looks set to be an exciting one for Arsenal. The Gunners have landed Bruno Guimaraes for a fee of £75million after a lengthy transfer saga, tying the Newcastle captain down to a five-year deal.

‌



Having secured their primary midfield target, manager Mikel Arteta and sporting director Andrea Berta are expected to turn their full attention to bringing in a defender and a marquee forward signing after being linked with several big names.

It comes after the Premier League champions added some crucial squad depth early on in the window. They've already signed Piero Hincapie in a £34.5m permanent deal, back-up goalkeeper Illan Meslier as a free agent and winger Christos Tzolis for £34m as Leandro Trossard's replacement.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino issues grovelling apology for botched World Cup plot after crisis meeting
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino issues grovelling apology for botched World Cup plot after crisis meeting

Gianni Infantino has been under fire for the last week after FIFA's controversial plan to sell off its competitions, including the World Cup, to private investors came to light

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino has been forced to apologise (Image: Tasos Katopodis - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

Grovelling Gianni Infantino has apologised for attempting to sell the World Cup, confirming that the controversial plan has been SCRAPPED. Infantino has faced intense backlash since FIFA announced last week - after media reports broke the news - a proposal for its competitions to be sold to private investors, sparking anger among the football community at all levels.

‌



UEFA members unanimously voted to boycott FIFA tournaments if the plan was allowed to go ahead, while FIFA chief Arsene Wenger spoke out against it. A crisis meeting was held in Morocco on Wednesday amid the unrelenting criticism and constant leaks regarding the plans.

‌



And now Infantino has admitted defeat with an apology - although he plans to fight on and remain FIFA President, despite widespread calls for him to resign. A letter signed by both Infantino and the FIFA General Secretary, Mattias Grafstrom, reads: "We acknowledge that errors were also made after the proposal was leaked to media.

‌



"We sincerely apologise for these errors and commit to them not happening again. With this in mind, we will conduct a necessary review, and a report will be presented to the FIFA Council at its next scheduled meeting."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Rusty Arsenal suffer friendly defeat as Mikel Arteta dealt injury blow - 5 talking points READ MORE :

Newcastle finally confirm Matthias Jaissle as new manager to replace Eddie Howe READ MORE :

The letter adds that Grafstrom and FIFA's Management Board 'reaffirm their full support' for Infantino, who's up for re-election next March. It goes on to say: "With the project withdrawn, FIFA will no longer tolerate any attacks on its integrity, good governance and due process and will take all necessary measures to protect and safeguard its name and reputation."

‌



Meanwhile, FIFA say that its leadership held a constructive and positive meeting in Rabat. It comes after a bombshell report claiming that Infantino had offered Morocco the chance to host 2030 World Cup final - which they're co-hosting with Spain and Portugal - if they agreed to his plan.

Should Gianni Infantino resign? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images FIFA's plan to sell off the World Cup has been scrapped (Image: Evrim Aydin/Anadolu via Getty Images)

‌



Any federations who backed the scheme were told that they would receive £30million, a portion of which would be available in January if they responded positively by a September deadline. Infantino was even accused of bribery by the president of the Jordan FA, who hit out on social media.

Prince Ali bin Al Hussein posted: "We pride ourselves in Jordan in upholding ethical values. We did not endorse him before and certainly will not now. But the whole situation amounts to blackmail and we refuse to give in to that."

Sports.title: Rusty Arsenal suffer friendly defeat as Mikel Arteta dealt injury blow - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Rusty Arsenal suffer friendly defeat as Mikel Arteta dealt injury blow - 5 talking points

ARSENAL 1-3 REAL BETIS: The Gunners were convincingly beaten in Dublin, giving Mikel Arteta some cause for concern ahead of his team's season which starts in just 11 days' time

View 5 Images Mikel Arteta will be disappointed with Arsenal's result and performance (Image: Charles McQuillan/Getty Images)

Lacklustre Arsenal fell to a comprehensive 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in their second pre-season friendly. The Gunners gave their fans in Dublin little to enjoy with an under-par display.

‌



Mikel Arteta watched his side make a string of mistakes, showing the kind of rustiness that he'll hope will be gone in less than a fortnight when they start the 2026-27 season against Manchester City for the Community Shield. Arsenal found themsleves 2-0 down inside 26 minutes and Arteta was visibly frustrated on the touchline.

‌



Piero Hincapie pulled one back but Betis didn't take long to restore their two-goal advantage before half-time. A raft of changes didn't make much difference in the second half and it was a match that will have fans talking for the wrong reasons.

‌



Here are five talking points from the Aviva Stadium.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Real Madrid change Vinicius Jr stance as Arsenal transfer hopes suffer blow READ MORE :

1. Kepa's clangers

With Illan Meslier through the door, there's competition to be Arsenal's No.2 goalkeeper. But Kepa Arrizabalaga didn't help his case by making an error in the ninth minute.

‌



A corner was floated in by Pablo Fornals and Kepa came steaming out looking to punch. But the Spaniard got it all wrong and completely missed the ball, giving Rodrigo Riquelme a tap-in.

Kepa's appeals for a foul fell on deaf ears and soon enough he made another error. His poor clearance surrendered possession to Betis and Nelson Deossa punished him with an unstoppable strike.

Will Arsenal win the Premier League? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

‌



View 5 Images Arsenal got off to a nightmare start (Image: Evan Treacy/Getty Images)

2. Still Set Piece FC

After finding themselves 2-0 down and playing poorly, Arsenal needed a response. That came in the form of - you guessed it - a corner.

New signing Christos Tzolis whipped the ball in and it evaded flapping Betis goalkeeper Alvaro Valles inside his own six-yard box. Standing a matter of inches from the line, Hincapie had a simple task to nod the ball in.

‌



It was another well-worked routine from the Gunners. Tzolis' delivery dipped perfectly and Betis were bamboozled by the runners in yellow, who were sporting Arsenal's new third kit.

View 5 Images Piero Hincapie pulled a goal back from a corner (Image: Paul Faith/AFP via Getty Images)

3. Guimaraes required

On the day Arsenal agreed a £75million deal to sign Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle, their second-choice midfield was exposed. Sloppy, lethargic, careless - all of those could be thrown at the trio of Ethan Nwaneri, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Kai Havertz.

‌



Both Betis' second and third goals summed up their performances that will remind the Arsenal board just why they're buying Guimaraes. Deossa's strike may've been a screamer but he was afforded was too much time to pull the trigger.

And then for Fornals' goal which restored Betis' two-goal cushion, Havertz gave the ball away with a weak pass. It was all far too easy and so unlike Arsenal.

View 5 Images Kai Havertz's mistake proved costly (Image: Charles McQuillan/Getty Images)

‌



4. Injury blow for teenager

Arteta rung in the changes at half-time, making a total of seven substitutions. One who came on was Louie Copley, who captained Arsenal's under-21 side last season aged 19.

But sadly for the highly-rated midfielder, who was used at right-back, his night only last 10 minutes. Copley had landed awkwardly while chasing the ball and immediately looked in pain.

Arteta reluctantly subbed him, as the teenager had to be helped off the pitch as he struggled to put weight on his leg. Hopefully for Copley, it's nothing serious.

‌



View 5 Images Louie Copley succumbed to injury 10 minutes after coming on (Image: Charles McQuillan/Getty Images)

5. Arteta managing minutes

As the game petered out, albeit with Betis looking the more likely to score against a youth Arsenal XI, Arteta made two intriguing substitutions. Gabriel Magalhaes and Gabriel Martinelli had only entered the fray at half-time, but they came off 30 minutes later.

The two Brazilians had only reached the round of 16 at the World Cup, but it's clear that Arteta is being careful with his starters who played a mammoth amount of minutes last season. Both Gabriels should be involved on Saturday at home to Borussia Dortmund.

Sports.title: Aoibheann Clarke, 16, dies after collapsing while playing in football cup final in front of dad
Sports.content:
Aoibheann Clarke, 16, dies after collapsing while playing in football cup final in front of dad

Aoibheann Clarke, 16, collapsed as the match entered extra time and was rushed to hospital in an ambulance — her dad was officiating the game in Taghmon, Ireland as assistant referee

View 2 Images Aoibheann Clarke, 16, died after collapsing during a final (Image: Wexford Youths Womens Football Club/Facebook)

A 16-year-old girl has tragically died after collapsing during a football final.

‌



Aoibheann Clarke, 16, was given CPR on the pitch while playing in the Girls Minor Division 6 Shield Gaelic football final in Taghmon, Ireland on Tuesday night. She was rushed to hospital in ambulance, but died a short time later.

‌



Eyewitnesses told local media that spectators' attention had been on an on-field clash between two players as the game went into extra time, before the alarm was raised over the 16-year-old girl's condition at the other end of the pitch.

‌



A number of people rushed on to the pitch to help, with Aoibheann said to have started breathing again after several minutes of chest compressions.

View 2 Images The talented youngster played for a Gaelic Athletic Association team and a football side (Image: Declan Clarke/Facebook)

Her dad had been officiating as linesman during the game, reported Irish national broadcaster RTE.

‌



Paramedics, police , fire crews, and an air ambulance all attended the scene.

The game was abandoned and her teammates at Taghmon Camross Gaelic football team stayed back at the club to wait for further news, before coaches told them she had died in hospital.

She was not known to have any underlying health conditions.

‌



In a statement, her club Taghmon Camross said: "At this incredibly difficult time, we would like to express our sincere gratitude to everyone who responded so quickly and compassionately to the emergency.

"Our heartfelt thanks go to the spectators who assisted, the first responders, the ambulance service, garda and the fire crew for their professionalism, care, and support.

"Our thoughts and prayers remain with our player's family, friends, teammates, coaches, and all who knew and loved her. We ask that everyone respects the family's privacy as they grieve this devastating loss.

‌



Aoibheann was also a talented footballer, and played for All Blacks AFC and Wexford FC.

A few weeks before she died, she had helped Wexford FC to victory in the Football Association of Ireland's Women's U19 Inter-League title.

Local sports club Wexford Camogie wrote in a tribute on Facebook: "Today, our thoughts are firmly with our friends in Wexford Ladies Football and with everyone in the Taghmon Camross Club.

‌



"Wexford Camogie is deeply saddened by the heartbreaking passing of Aoibheann Clarke, a talented 16-year-old player with her whole life ahead of her.

"We extend our heartfelt and sincere condolences to Aoibheann's family, her friends, her teammates, her club, and to everyone who had the privilege of knowing her.

"Wexford Camogie also has the Ferns Club and the Referee in our thoughts today. We acknowledge that it was a very difficult evening for all concerned, and we are thinking of them also at this incredibly sad and difficult time.

Article continues below

"May Aoibheann rest in eternal peace. She will forever be remembered by those who loved her, played alongside her, and cherished her.

"The final whistle has blown, but your spirit will forever live on in every game played."

Sports.title: Newcastle finally confirm Matthias Jaissle as new manager to replace Eddie Howe
Sports.content:
Newcastle finally confirm Matthias Jaissle as new manager to replace Eddie Howe

Newcastle quickly identified Al-Ahli boss Matthias Jaissle as their top target to replace Eddie Howe, but the announcement of his appointment was delayed - until now

View 2 Images Matthias Jaissle has been confirmed by Newcastle (Image: FC Red Bull Salzburg via Getty Images)

Newcastle have finally confirmed the appointment of Matthias Jaissle as their new manager. Jaissle, 38, arrives from Saudi Arabian club Al-Ahli, with Newcastle paying a £9.5million compensation fee.

‌



The German replaces Eddie Howe, who shockingly resigned midway through pre-season last week. Jaissle has already been working with Newcastle's squad in La Manga, Spain for the last few days.

‌



But Al-Ahli wanted to delay the announcement until 7pm on Wednesday. Jaissle spent three years in Saudi Arabia following spells with Red Bull Salzburg and Liefering in Austria.

‌



The 38-year-old guided Al-Ahli - who are owned by Newcastle's owners, the Saudi Public Investment Fund - to winning the Asian Champions League in each of the last two seasons. But Jaissle has decided to move to St James' Park, kicking off a new era.

"When Newcastle United comes your way, you take notice," he commented in Newcastle's announcement. "The ambition of the club, the vision for the future and the opportunity ahead made this an incredibly compelling place to be.

‌



"I have followed the club's journey closely in recent years and the progress that has been made is clear for everyone to see. I am incredibly excited about the future. I fully and unreservedly believe in this project, the ambition and the direction the club is taking.

"There is a clear vision, strong leadership and an exceptional platform to build on. My teams are built on togetherness, hard work, intensity and a passion to improve every single day.

"I will bring full commitment, full energy and a determination to give everything I have to help this club achieve its ambitions. I believe there is enormous potential within this squad and throughout the football club.

‌



Will Matthias Jaissle be a success at Newcastle? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

View 2 Images Matthias Jaissle won the Asian Champions League twice (Image: Getty Images)

"I am excited to work with the players, staff and leadership team to help take the club forward. I cannot wait to get started and will attack this opportunity. I give my complete commitment and total energy to bringing further success to Newcastle United."

‌



Sporting director Ross Wilson added: "Matthias' leadership style and football philosophy are strongly aligned with our sporting vision. His teams play high-energy football and we could feel his passion during all of our discussions throughout the recruitment process.

"He has consistently demonstrated an ability to improve players, build cohesive teams and create elite performance environments in his coaching career.

"His successes at Salzburg and Al-Ahli underline his ability to deliver results while developing a clear football identity. We believe he is uniquely positioned to build on the strong foundations already in place and help take Newcastle United forward."

Jaissle's first Premier League game in charge will be at home to Liverpool on Sunday, August 23.

Sports.title: Real Madrid change Vinicius Jr stance as Arsenal transfer hopes suffer blow
Sports.content:
Real Madrid change Vinicius Jr stance as Arsenal transfer hopes suffer blow

Real Madrid are continuing to hold talks with Vinicius Jr and his entourage, while Arsenal are waiting in the wings hoping to pull off a sensational transfer swoop

View 2 Images Arsenal are going all out to sign Vinicius Junior (Image: Antonio Villalba/Real Madrid via Getty Images)

Real Madrid have made Vinicius Jr an improved contract offer in a bid to fend off interest from Arsenal. Vinicius, 26, has entered the final year of his current deal in Madrid and the Gunners are willing to offer him a lucrative move to London.

‌



Arsenal would be willing to make the Brazilian their highest-paid player and boss Mikel Arteta is believed to have spoken to him. On Wednesday, talks between Vinicius' camp, Real general director Jose Angel Sanchez and chief scout Juni Calafat took place.

‌



The two parties had previously been far apart in negotiations, with Vinicius demanding an eye-watering salary of €28m (£24m). According to The Athletic, Real have now raised their offer to a level which they believe reflects the forward's importance.

‌



Vinicius' decision on the proposal will either bring an end to the saga over his future or let it rumble on. Should no agreement be found, Real would have to decide whether to sell him this summer or risk letting him leave as a free agent next year.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



How Arsenal could line up after signing Bruno Guimaraes and completing Vinicius Jr transfer READ MORE :

If Vinicius does stay at the La Liga giants, he'll be owed a substantial loyalty bonus which is reportedly worth around £9m. New Real manager Jose Mourinho wants the 26-year-old to stay, as he aims to make a successful return to the Bernabeu.

On Tuesday, Vinicius gave an interview to Real Madrid TV about working under Mourinho. "It has ⁠gone very well, getting to know the new coach and the new players, and training very hard," he said. "Mourinho wants me to be as I have always been: happy, cheerful ‌and playing my football."

Mikel Arteta could be asked about Arsenal's pursuit of Vinicius when his side face Real Betis in a friendly in Dublin on Wednesday. It comes after Arsenal agreed a £75m deal with Newcastle for Bruno Guimaraes, Vinicius' international team-mate.

‌



The Gunners beat Girona 4-1 in their opening pre-season friendly thanks to goals from Kai Havertz, Christos Tzolis, Max Dowman and Gabriel Jesus. Tszolis remains Arsenal's only outfield signing so far, with the Greek winger joining from Club Brugge for £34m.

Will Vinicius Jr stay or go? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

View 2 Images Real Madrid's offer is bad news for Arsenal (Image: Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

‌



Arteta has also welcomed a new goalkeeper. French shot-stopper Illan Meslier arrived on a free transfer, having been released by Leeds.

After playing Betis, Arsenal will host two friendlies at the Emirates against Borussia Dortmund and Como. Their first game of the season will be the Community Shield against Manchester City, who Arsenal pipped to the Premier League title last term.

The Gunners kick-off their league campaign by facing newly-promoted Coventry at home on Friday, August 21. Arteta's side then travel to Aston Villa.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
