NEW DELHI: The death toll from the devastating floods in Assam rose to 95 after six more people died, while more than 1.6 lakh people remained affected across 14 districts, officials said on Thursday.According to the Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA), six deaths were reported on Wednesday, two each in Sivasagar and Biswanath districts, and one each in Golaghat and Morigaon.Sivasagar continues to be the worst-affected district, accounting for 50 of the 95 deaths reported so far.Neighbouring Charaideo has recorded 21 fatalities, followed by Jorhat (9), Golaghat (5), Dhemaji (3), Karbi Anglong (2) and Biswanath (2). One death each has also been reported from Sonitpur, Kamrup Metropolitan and Morigaon.The floods have affected over 1,60,600 people in Biswanath, Charaideo, Darrang, Dhemaji, Golaghat, Jorhat, Kamrup Metropolitan, Karbi Anglong, Lakhimpur, Nagaon, Sivasagar, Sonitpur, Tinsukia and Udalguri districts.Sivasagar alone has around 57,000 affected residents, followed by Golaghat (34,000) and Jorhat (25,000).The number of affected people has risen sharply from 1.22 lakh in five districts reported on Tuesday.Authorities have set up more than 100 relief camps and relief distribution centres across six districts, where 44,523 people are currently taking shelter.Floodwaters have submerged 16,951.76 hectares of cropland, while embankments, roads, bridges and other public infrastructure have suffered extensive damage in several parts of the state.Union health and family welfare minister J P Nadda, who was deputed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, visited the flood-hit Nepalikhuti area along the Assam-Nagaland border in Sivasagar district on Wednesday, one of the regions worst affected by the latest wave of floods that began on July 19.Later in the day, Nadda chaired a high-level review meeting with Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma and senior state officials to assess the flood situation and review ongoing relief, rehabilitation and healthcare measures."I have visited the flood-hit Nepalikhuti area. Along with CM Sarma, I have witnessed the scale of devastation. The damage is so huge that it will take time (for normalcy to return)," Nadda told reporters after interacting with flood-affected families."The Central Government and the State Government have stood with complete sensitivity and utmost promptness beside every flood-affected family. We are continuing the relief and rehabilitation efforts with full commitment. I assure everyone that there will be no lapses of any kind in the relief and rescue operations. Teams of Central Government representatives are conducting extensive assessments of the flood damages, and all kinds of financial assistance are being extended," he added.Nadda is scheduled to visit Yazali in Arunachal Pradesh on Thursday to inspect areas affected by flash floods and interact with affected residents. During the visit, Nadda will chair a review meeting with state government officials to assess the health situation and review ongoing relief and rehabilitation efforts in the region.The visit is part of his three-day tour of the Northeast from August 4 to 6.

World.title: 'Not fluent in Tamil is an insult': Actor Dhanush pushes for mother tongue first
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Actor Dhanush has renewed the focus on the language debate with his remarks stressing the importance of learning Tamil and being "fluent in one's mother tongue."

Speaking at an event, the actor strongly backed the Tamil language and urged people to prioritise fluency in their mother tongue.

Recalling his school days, Dhanush said, "When I was in school, we were fluent in Tamil and we struggled with English. Now the situation is opposite."

He added, "Now, out of the 10 people I meet, eight don't know Tamil. One should be fluent in their mother tongue before everything else. To say I'm not fluent in Tamil is not a matter of pride. It's an insult. Focus on learning Tamil language."

His remarks come amid the long-running language debate in Tamil Nadu, where the issue has frequently put the state government at odds with the Centre. Leaders across the state's political spectrum, from DMK chief and former CM MK Stalin to TVK founder and CM Vijay, have repeatedly accused the Centre of attempting to impose Hindi on southern states.

World.title: Bombay high court convicts Tarun Tejpal in 2013 rape case, overturns acquittal
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Bombay high court on Thursday convicted former Tehelka editor-in-chief

in the 2013 rape case filed by his former junior colleague, overturning his acquittal by a Goa trial court.

The verdict came nearly 13 years after the alleged incident during the ThinkFest event in Goa, where Tejpal was accused of sexually assaulting a junior colleague inside a hotel elevator. The high court had reserved its judgment last week after hearing arguments from both sides.

Arguments on the quantum of sentence are currently underway, and the court is scheduled to pronounce its order on sentencing at around 2.30 pm.

The Goa government had challenged Tejpal's acquittal after a sessions court cleared him of all charges in May 2021. The appeal was heard by Justices Dr Neela Gokhale and Amit Jamsandekar of the Bombay high court's Goa bench, which had directed Tejpal to remain present for the pronouncement of the verdict.

Appearing for the Goa government, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta had argued that the trial court committed a serious error by evaluating the complainant's conduct based on preconceived notions of how a survivor of sexual assault should behave.





He submitted that there is no universal standard governing the reaction of a sexual assault survivor, as responses vary depending on an individual's education, personality, social background and circumstances.

Tejpal, who was present in court, sought leniency, claiming that he was a "political victim" and the father of two daughters.

Mehta also argued that the trial court placed undue emphasis on minor inconsistencies in the complainant's statements instead of examining whether her core allegations remained consistent.

Referring to an email sent by Tejpal to the complainant after the alleged incident, the Solicitor General argued that the accused had apologised for his "lapse of judgment", expressed shame and stated that he believed the encounter had been consensual. According to the prosecution, those statements amounted to an admission that an encounter had taken place.

The defence, led by senior advocate Abad Ponda, argued that the prosecution had misread the apology emails as admissions of a sexual encounter.

Ponda submitted that none of the emails contained any admission of a consensual physical or sexual encounter and that the references related only to a consensual verbal conversation of a sexual nature.

The defence also questioned the complainant's credibility, arguing that her conduct before and after the alleged incident, along with emails, WhatsApp messages and documentary evidence, contradicted the prosecution's case.

NEW DELHI: Air India's recent severe turbulence incident is now under a "thorough investigation" by the directorate general of civil aviation (DGCA), civil aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu said on Wednesday.Naidu said the Air India flight from Phuket to New Delhi experienced severe turbulence for "four to five minutes", leaving several passengers injured and some crew members with spinal and neck injuries.At least 17 people, including four cabin crew members, were injured after the aircraft suddenly lost around 300 feet in altitude during the midair turbulence.Addressing the media, Naidu said the aircraft was secured immediately after landing and all crucial evidence has been taken into the regulator's custody."In terms of why the incident has happened, we have immediately alerted the DGCA to thoroughly investigate the situation. The moment the plane was landed, it was put in a separate hangar. The data recorder, the voice recorder, everything is in the possession of DGCA. They will thoroughly investigate how and why this incident happened. Only when we have the facts in front of us, we are going to make it public," he said.The minister said medical teams attended to passengers and crew immediately after the flight landed in Delhi."The moment the flight landed in Delhi, the medical assistance team immediately attended to them. All first aid and medical assistance that needed to be provided was done at the airport itself. There were some passengers and crew members who were observed to need more medical assistance, they were shifted to Medanta Hospital and also Fortis Hospital," Naidu added.He said seven passengers admitted to Medanta Hospital on Monday were discharged after undergoing medical examinations."Spinal Injuries Centre, Fortis Centre - two passsengers were admitted yesterday. They both were also discharged but four crew members were admitted in Fortis where I also personally visited along with Ministry Team and DGCA Team. We interacted with crew members also. They have been very brave, even after that incident happened for 5 minutes and they were prone to certain injuries, the plane had to travel for 1 more hour. Even through that hour, the crew members provided all the assistance that was required. So, it was very brave of the women, the crew members who were on the flight," he said.The Airbus A320neo, operating as flight AI2379 from Phuket to Delhi on Tuesday, was carrying 137 passengers and eight crew members. Following the turbulence, 13 passengers and four crew members sustained injuries and were taken to hospitals for medical evaluation.According to Air India, as of 6:50 pm, five passengers had been discharged, while the remaining injured continued to receive treatment and care.An Air India spokesperson said on Tuesday, "Earlier today, Air India flight AI2379 operating from Phuket to Delhi experienced a sudden loss of altitude during cruise. After the momentary event, the aircraft continued normally and landed safely in Delhi at 11:07 hrs IST."The DGCA is now investigating the incident to determine the cause of the severe midair turbulence.

World.title: Centre deploys national team as Chandipura outbreak probe intensifies
World.content:
NEW DELHI: With 35 laboratory-confirmed Chandipura virus infections and 22 deaths among 184 suspected cases reported in children under 15 across Gujarat this monsoon, and the virus also affecting children from neighbouring Rajasthan, the Centre on Wednesday deployed a National Joint Outbreak Response Team (NJORT) to strengthen outbreak investigations and accelerate scientific efforts to contain the disease.

Chandipura virus, a sandfly-borne virus that primarily affects children, can rapidly progress from fever to

(AES), a severe brain infection. While sandflies are the established vector, scientists are investigating whether mosquitoes, ticks or mites may also be involved in the current outbreak.

The virus is not new to India. First identified in Chandipura village in Maharashtra in 1965, it has caused periodic outbreaks of acute encephalitis among children in states such as Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat, particularly during the monsoon.

The multidisciplinary team, comprising experts from the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) and the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), will support state authorities in outbreak investigation, epidemiological assessment, laboratory coordination, clinical management and vector surveillance. The NCDC's Public Health Emergency Operations Centre has also been activated to coordinate the response.





Rajasthan has stepped up surveillance after children from the state, including a two-year-old girl, tested positive for Chandipura virus while undergoing treatment in Gujarat. The cross-border cases prompted the Centre to include Rajasthan in its coordinated response.

The deployment comes amid one of the country's most extensive scientific investigations into Chandipura virus in recent years, involving multiple ICMR institutes, the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and the Gujarat Biotechnology Research Centre (GBRC).

Scientists are trying to answer key questions about the virus's transmission, clinical spectrum and evolution while generating evidence to guide public health measures.

Surveillance has been intensified among patients with acute febrile illness (AFI) and acute encephalitis syndrome, while community serosurveys are underway to estimate the extent of asymptomatic infections. Researchers are also analysing samples from sandflies, mosquitoes, ticks and mites to identify the vector responsible for the current outbreak.

At the same time, blood and milk samples from cattle, buffaloes and goats are being tested to determine whether domestic animals could act as virus reservoirs.

Around 70 animal blood samples have been collected so far and are being analysed for Chandipura virus and other relevant pathogens.

Scientists are also carrying out whole-genome sequencing of virus samples to determine whether the circulating strain has undergone genetic changes. Officials said findings from the investigation, together with data generated through India's hospital-based Acute Encephalitis Syndrome surveillance network, will strengthen outbreak detection, improve understanding of the disease and support evidence-based public health interventions.

World.title: Jharkhand protests: Five-member student panel to hold talks with Soren govt today - key points
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Students protesting alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations in Jharkhand have agreed in principle to hold talks with the state government, provided the discussions take place in the presence of the media.

The development came even as the Crime Investigation Department (CID) arrested five more people in connection with the alleged recruitment scam, taking the investigation forward.

Student leader Radhe Kumar said a five-member core committee would attend the meeting with government representatives. "Five members of our core team will attend the meeting. We will present our demands to the government through the SDO, who will convey them to the appropriate authorities.

Once the government responds to our demands, we will decide our next course of action," he said.

Here are the top developments:

Students agree to talks, but seek public meeting

Student leaders said they were prepared to send a four- or five-member delegation for discussions after receiving a message from the government through the Sub-Divisional Officer (SDO). However, they insisted that the talks should be transparent.

"We also had another demand: if the chief minister comes out to speak with us publicly in front of live media on an open platform, a proper resolution could be reached.





In our previous protest, our representatives were taken into a closed room, and nothing came out of it. They are calling a five-member team just to stall and suppress our movement," one protester alleged.

Another protester echoed the demand, saying, "The chief minister should listen to the students' demands in front of the press and media, and whatever promises he intends to fulfil should be stated publicly. For the last 26 years in Jharkhand, students' issues have been heard in closed rooms, and the files have remained closed forever."

Student leader Ravindra Paswan said both sides had shown willingness to engage.

"The government has expressed its willingness to engage in dialogue, and we have also conveyed our willingness. Dialogue is essential in a democratic country as it is the only way to reach a resolution," Paswan said.

He added that the students had placed two conditions before the government.

"Our primary condition is that the dialogue should take place directly with the chief minister, and we have been assured that the chief minister will be present.

Secondly, we want at least two media representatives to be present during the discussions. The SDO has asked us to submit the names of our delegation members before 10 am, after which the date and time of the meeting will be communicated," he said.

Government says doors are open

The state government has repeatedly stressed its willingness to engage with the protesters.

Jharkhand minister Irfan Ansari said, "The chief minister has constituted the committee...

We have opened the door for dialogue. Talks will take place, we will listen to your demands, and if they are reasonable, we will certainly accept them. They are our students, our children." He also accused the BJP of trying to politicise the issue.

Rural development minister Deepika Pandey Singh said a committee had been formed and students had been asked to nominate their representatives so discussions could begin.

However, Finance Minister Radhakrishna Kishore clarified that the ministers' group was only monitoring the agitation and was not a formal negotiation committee. He said the chief minister remained sensitive to the students' concerns and that the government was ready for talks whenever the students decided to engage.

Earlier this week, chief minister Hemant Soren also said the government was open to dialogue and assured students that their demands would be considered seriously.

"...Many individuals have already been arrested and sent to jail, and investigative agencies are conducting raids at multiple locations. Overall, the agencies are working diligently and effectively on this matter, and I believe we will move forward towards a concrete resolution..." he said.

"The government's doors are open to everyone. Anyone who has demands can come forward and present their concerns. We are already aware of the issues to some extent, and if they present their views, the government will certainly consider them seriously," he added.

Probe gathers pace as arrests rise

The CID's latest action saw five more arrests in connection with the alleged examination irregularities, taking the total number of arrests to 19.

The investigation is being led by an SIT, which is examining digital records, application logs and other evidence to establish the extent of the alleged recruitment irregularities.

World.title: Air India turbulence scare: After the drop, the trauma lingers
World.content:
Doctors say the physical and mental toll can last for months (Photo: ANI).

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Air India flight from Phuket to Delhi that suddenly dropped nearly 300 feet after encountering severe turbulence on Tuesday has once again highlighted that the impact of such incidents extends well beyond visible injuries. While at least 14 passengers and cabin crew members were injured and the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has launched an investigation, doctors say the physical and psychological consequences of severe turbulence can linger for days, weeks or even months.Psychiatrists warn that even passengers who escape with minor or no physical injuries may develop significant psychological distress. "The sudden perception of imminent danger, combined with the loss of control and visible panic, can activate the body's survival response," said Dr Rajesh Sagar, professor in the Department of Psychiatry at AIIMS.Dr Sagar said that passengers may experience persistent fear, anxiety, sleep disturbances, intrusive memories and heightened alertness after the incident. In some cases, the experience can trigger Acute Stress Disorder (ASD) within days, which may progress to Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) if symptoms persist beyond a month."The psychological impact should not be underestimated simply because there are no major physical injuries," Dr Sagar said.He advised passengers to seek help if they continue to experience nightmares, flashbacks, avoidance of flying or emotional distress. Early psychological support based on the principles of Psychological First Aid can reduce the risk of long-term trauma, he added.Doctors also cautioned against dismissing apparently minor physical injuries sustained during turbulence. Dr (Maj.) Mukesh Garg, Director of Orthopaedics, Arthroscopy and Sports Injury at Sarvodaya Hospital, said passengers thrown against seats, overhead bins or cabin interiors may sustain bruises, ligament injuries, fractures or injuries to the neck and spine."Not all injuries become obvious immediately," he said. "Soft tissue injuries, ligament tears and mild concussions may take several hours to become apparent. Pain, swelling and stiffness often worsen over the next 24 to 48 hours."He advised anyone who suffered a blow to the head, neck or back to undergo medical evaluation even if symptoms initially appear mild. Warning signs requiring immediate medical attention include severe or worsening headache, repeated vomiting, dizziness, confusion, blurred vision, weakness or numbness of the limbs, difficulty walking, severe neck pain and loss of bladder or bowel control.Experts also recommend that passengers who develop a fear of flying after severe turbulence gradually rebuild confidence through counselling, breathing exercises and relaxation techniques. Starting with shorter flights, travelling with a trusted companion and keeping the seatbelt fastened throughout the journey can also help restore a sense of safety and control.

World.title: Operation intensified to capture tiger on the prowl in Eluru region of A.P.
World.content:
The Andhra Pradesh Forest Department has stepped up efforts to safely capture the tiger that has been on the prowl across forest areas in Eluru, Rajamahendravaram, Kakinada, Chinturu and the Papikonda National Park region.

Experts from the Bengaluru-based Wildlife SOS organisation and the Wardha unit of People for Animals have been deployed, along with experienced personnel from various tiger reserves. Six trained tranquilliser shooters have been kept on standby.

According to forest officials, the tiger has displayed exceptional agility and caution, avoiding areas with human activity and even locations where observation platforms, known as machans, have been erected. Despite these challenges, expert teams have been working round the clock to trace the animal.

The department has adopted several advanced search and tracking methods based on pugmarks, camera-trap footage and location data.

Officials have divided the operational zone into inner and outer rectangles as part of a double-rectangle strategy aimed at restricting the tiger’s movement. Baits and traps have been placed to lure the animal into a designated area where tranquilliser teams and veterinary experts are waiting.

Nearly 350 personnel from territorial and wildlife divisions, along with local villagers, have been involved in the operation. Communication is being maintained through walkie-talkies and a VHF communication network.

Forest teams are also employing star-pattern and U-shaped search methods to monitor the possible routes taken by the tiger. Thermal drones, night-vision cameras, tracking teams and net fencing are being used to improve the chances of capturing the animal safely.

The department has been monitoring the tiger’s movement. It has alerted residents of Darbhagudem, P. Rajavaram, Chellavarigudem, A. Polavaram, Appalarajugudem, Sirivarigudem, Ramannapalem, Madakavarigudem, Datlavarigudem, Sriratnagudem, Sitampeta and nearby villages through drum announcements and public address systems.

Officials from the Kannapuram, Polavaram, Kukkunoor and Jangareddygudem forest ranges have been placed on high alert. The department has appealed to residents to remain calm, follow official instructions and cooperate with the authorities until the operation is completed.

Chief Conservator of Forests (Rajamahendravaram) T. Jyothi and Eluru District Forest Officer P.V. Sandeep Reddy are supervising the operation and reviewing the measures being undertaken on the ground.

World.title: Bihar model schools makeover: Principals vow to follow renaming, repainting directives
World.content:
In view of the Bihar government’s recent decision to repaint and rename all 551 model schools from class 9-12 in all blocks of the State as “Saraswati Vidya Niketan”, the schools have started painting the exterior walls with the instructed paint of “sunrise” colour, which prominently looks as saffron with which the ruling Bhartiya Janata Party (BJP) identifies with.

The exterior walls of B.P. High School in Begusarai, where Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, along with State Education Minister Mithilesh Tiwari, had visited on July 19, 2026, and announced the renaming and repainting of all the model schools, were painted with the “sunrise” colour. The instructed name was also printed on polymer plastic sheets, by spending lakhs of rupees in “just three-days haste”. However, school principal Kamini Kumari wondered why the schools, that were painted afresh only few days ago, had to be repainted by a new government’s directive.

“We’re the lowest-rung employees of the department, teaching in government schools and we’ve to follow whatever directive or guideline comes from above. I had done fresh painting of my school building a few days ago, spending lakhs of rupees, but again we’ve been asked to repaint it with the sunrise color and the first coat of the paint has already been done,” the school principal, who also teaches chemistry, told The Hindu on August 4, 2026.

The main gate of the century-old school, established in the year 1888, displays a board renaming it as “Saraswati Vidya Niketan” (Model School), B.P. Inter School, Begusarai. “From July 16-18, we engaged nearly 50 workers for a fresh coat of the suggested colour and we did our work ahead of the Chief Minister’s visit,” added the principal of the school, which is spread across about five-acres of land in middle of the Begusarai town.

There are 44 teachers in the school with 2,900 students from Class 9-12. “It’s a big school. The Chief Minister, who visited the school along with other top officials, was visibly impressed with the presentation of the students,” said the school principal. Her husband Bishwajeet Kumar, who is a sports teacher, is busy making a new cricket pitch on school campus. “We’ll make it happen this too very soon. The intermittent rain these days is the only constraint, otherwise, we’re getting all support from the district administration,” he said.

The District Education Officer (DEO) Manoj Kumar said, “In the Begusarai district, there are 18 blocks but we’ve 4 extra model schools as the district is big. Work is going on in every model school, as per the guidelines of the department.”

“We have already spent nearly ₹12 lakh on the school’s repaint, as per the guideline. The school had another colour only a few days ago,” said Mr. Kumar. The school will have a fresh coat of “sunrise colour”, though it looks more saffron than the sunrise and white from inside. “We still fail to understand why a fresh coat of colour of the exterior of the school building was suggested, spending lakhs of rupees. It would have been better if the amount was spent on increasing the number of the computer sets in the school from 10 to 50, giving access to each student of a class to learn something,” said another teacher, on condition of anonymity.

Govt’s instructions to schools

The Bihar State Educational Infrastructure Development Corporation Ltd. (BSIEDC), which primarily looks after renovation and construction work of government schools in Bihar, had issued a letter on July 7, 2026, to all district units of BSIEDC with subject related to paintings of the Saraswati Vidya Niketan (Model) Schools and suggested the colour code as: “External Wall — Sunrise (0526 — Asian Paint), Border: Chocolate Brown Enamel (Asian Paint), Interior — Xtra White (Asian Paint) and Door / Windows: Golden Brown Enamel (Asian Paint).” The letter instructed that the directive should be followed as “soon as possible”.

Nearly 130 km northwest of Begusarai, at Senduari Model School in Vaishali district, the repaint of the exterior walls was completed. The school was repainted just one day ago on July 18, a day before the CM and others reached Begusarai. “We engaged 14-15 workers to paint round-the-clock on that day to complete the work,” said school principal Krishna Kant Roy. “Only two-weeks ago, I had the school painted in sky blue colour but we had to repaint it following the government’s guidelines,” rued Mr. Roy.

However, he added, “We’ve to follow the guidelines, not to question the directive.” Asked how much money has been spent yet on the repainting, which looks prominently like saffron, Mr. Roy said, “So far, we’ve spent nearly a lakh rupee on the new paint.” When asked whether the government will reimburse the money, he said, “We’ve been asked to get the money reimbursed from the development fund of the school.” The government schools in Bihar charges around ₹25-30 as “development fees” from every student at the time of their admission. The school, established in 1968, has a total of 965 students and 32 teachers, including the principal.

“Earlier, schools in Bihar were painted either in pink, sky-blue or in white that were decent and identified from afar, but this new colour sunrise, which prominently looks saffron, has altogether got a distinct connotation,” said retired government school teacher Ramashray Prasad Singh.

Bihar has a total of 534 blocks across 38 districts, but some bigger districts such as Patna, Gaya, Begusarai, and Muzaffarpur have more than one model school, taking the number of such schools to 551.

World.title: Floodwaters recede in parts of central Kerala; IMD sounds orange alert in five districts
World.content:
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) on Thursday (August 6, 2026) issued an orange alert forecasting moderate rainfall and strong winds in five central Kerala districts even as floodwaters began receding in several affected areas, officials said.

The IMD issued the three-hour orange alert for Pathanamthitta, Alappuzha, Kottayam, Idukki and Ernakulam districts from 7 am to 10 am on Thursday.

According to the IMD statement, these districts are likely to receive moderate rainfall accompanied by surface wind speeds of up to 40 kmph over the next three hours.

Officials said floodwaters have started receding from several low-lying areas in Pathanamthitta, Kottayam and Ernakulam districts.

However, flooding continues in Upper Kuttanad and Kuttanad regions of Alappuzha district, although water levels have begun to decline gradually, they said.

According to the Alappuzha district administration, 118 relief camps are functioning in Cherthala, Ambalapuzha, Kuttanad, Karthikappally, Mavelikara and Chengannur taluks.

A total of 5,012 families comprising 14,646 people are staying in these relief camps, they said.

Major road links, including the Alappuzha-Changanassery road and the Ambalapuzha-Thiruvalla road, remain inundated, disrupting the movement of people and goods.

District administrations have declared holidays for educational institutions in flood-affected areas.

Earlier, the IMD had issued orange alerts for Pathanamthitta, Alappuzha, Kottayam, Idukki, Ernakulam, Kannur and Kasaragod districts for Thursday.

An orange alert for Malappuram, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Kannur and Kasaragod districts has been issued for Friday.

An orange alert indicates the likelihood of rainfall ranging from 115 mm to 204 mm.

The Kerala State Disaster Management Authority (KSDMA) advised people not to enter rivers and other water bodies for bathing, fishing or any other purpose during the heavy rains.

The authority also urged the public to avoid non-essential travel during periods of intense rainfall and refrain from visiting waterfalls, reservoirs and hilly tourist destinations until the weather warnings are withdrawn.

Caution advised

Motorists have been advised to exercise caution while travelling along roads near water bodies and on stretches undergoing repair work due to the increased risk of accidents during heavy rain.

The KSDMA also cautioned people against gathering on bridges over rivers and other water bodies for sightseeing or taking selfies and urged them to avoid night travel to hilly regions.

It further warned of accidents caused by uprooted trees and damaged electricity poles due to strong winds.

World.title: Parliament Monsoon Session Day 14 LIVE: Rajya Sabha adjourned till 2:15 p.m.; Opposition demands answers from Amit Shah
World.content:
Opposition MPs protested in Parliament House complex on Thursday (August 6, 2026) against the theft of donations at the Ram temple in Ayodhya and police excesses against student protestors.

The Lok Sabha is set to discuss the The Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, according to the agenda on Thursday (August 6, 2026). The Bill, which will be moved by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, seeks to amend the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, the Income-tax Act, 2025, and the Finance Act, 2026.

Parliament Monsoon Session Day 13 highlights: Rajya Sabha clears SC Judges’ Bill; Lok Sabha adjourned for the day

The Rajya Sabha will consider the Appropriation (No.3) Bill, 2026. It was approved by the Lok Sabha earlier. The legislation authorises the appropriation of money out of the Consolidated Fund of India to meet the amounts spent on certain services during the financial year ended on the 31st of March, 2023, in excess of the amounts granted for those services and for that year.

Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju met Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday (August 5, 2026) in an effort to break the parliamentary deadlock, with the two sides discussing the proposed delimitation Bill and the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment (FCRA) Bill, 2026.

World.title: Supreme Court stays arrest of Abhishek Banerjee's aide Sumit Roy in Salboni land-grabbing case
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Thursday stayed the arrest of Sumit Roy, Personal Assistant to Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee, in connection with the Salboni land-grabbing case.

Also Read | Calcutta High Court dismisses Abhishek Banerjee’s plea to visit abroad for eye treatment

The top court, however, directed him to cooperate fully with the ongoing investigation.

On August 3, the Calcutta High Court rejected the anticipatory bail plea of Mr. Roy in connection with the alleged government land fraud case being investigated by the Salboni Police.

The case was registered under penal provisions relating to cheating, criminal breach of trust, forgery, use of forged documents and criminal conspiracy.

On Thursday (August 6), a Bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohna took note of submissions of senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for Mr. Roy, in the case and protected him from from any coercive action.

"The petitioner to fully cooperate with the ongoing investigation. He should not be accompanied by any advocate or any other person. He shall remain available for any investigation from 10:00 am to 6:00 pm. with the usual breaks. However, his arrest will remain stayed," the Bench ordered.

Mr. Sankaranarayanan said that his client had already been granted anticipatory bail by the Calcutta High Court in another case relating to the alleged cash-for-jobs scam.

He also said that the FIR in the present case was registered only after the new government assumed office.

Opposing the plea, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the West Bengal government, said the alleged offence had been committed several years ago but no action had been taken by the previous government.

The Solicitor General also strongly opposed the grant of interim relief, saying that his custodial interrogation was necessary.

The law officer also said that attempts by law enforcement agencies to arrest the accused had previously been obstructed by former chief minister Mamata Banerjee.

He sought permission to place the relevant material on the affidavit.

World.title: Malabar Milma in Kerala announces ₹5-crore Onam bonus for dairy farmers
World.content:
Malabar Regional Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union (Malabar Milma) in Kerala will distribute ₹5.04 crore as an Onam gift to dairy farmers this season.

The package comprises ₹4.2 crore as an additional milk price payout and ₹84 lakh in cattle feed subsidies. Nearly 1,00,000 dairy farmers and around 1,200 primary Anand Pattern Co-operative Societies (APCOS) across the Malabar region will benefit from this initiative, Milma chairman K. S. Mani has said.

An additional milk price of ₹2 per litre will be paid for standard-quality milk supplied to the regional union via the APCOS between June 1 and 30. The additional price for the 210 lakh litres of milk collected during this period totals ₹4.2 crore, which will reach dairy farmers across Malabar’s six districts in the coming days. The decision was finalised during a meeting of the Malabar Milma board, he said.

​Under the subsidy scheme running throughout August, a discount of ₹100 per 50 kg bag will be provided for Milma Gomathy Gold and Milma Bipro cattle feed distributed through co-operative societies in the regional union.

Besides, a subsidy of ₹50 per bag will be offered on pelletised Total Mixed Ration feed from the Malabar Rural Development Foundation. In cases where feed supply is disrupted and societies purchase silage directly, a subsidy of 75 paise per kg for farmers and 25 paise per kg for societies has been announced.

​With this latest payout, the regional union has transferred ₹10 crore to farmers in this financial year alone, over and above the standard milk procurement prices, through additional milk price payouts and cattle feed subsidies.

​The additional milk price amount would be credited to the societies’ accounts alongside the milk payments due for August 1 to 10, and the societies will disburse these funds to the dairy farmers before Onam, Mr. Mani added.

(The writer, Aleesha V. Joseph is an intern with The Hindu)

World.title: What to see at Contemporary Now 2026 in Chennai: Exhibitions, talks and artist walkthroughs
World.content:
Art is not always something you stand quietly in front of. Sometimes, it spills into a cafe conversation, a studio visit, or even an entire city. This August, Chennai becomes a large gallery as Contemporary Now returns for its third edition, transforming museums, galleries, and cultural spaces, inviting visitors to wander, question, linger, and discover not just art, but the city itself.

The third edition brings together 66 artists from seven leading galleries, complemented by a city-wide programme of exhibitions, discussions, artist walkthroughs and workshops.

Running from August 8 to 25, Contemporary Now will be anchored at the Lalit Kala Akademi, with a series of partner programmes unfolding across Chennai. Work will be presented by seven leading galleries — Ashvita’s, Chemould Prescott Road, Chatterjee & Lal, Experimenter, Project 88, TARQ and Vadehra Art Gallery. This year’s edition is centred on the curatorial theme Practices in Continuum: Tracing the Present, exploring how contemporary artistic practices evolve through research, experimentation and dialogue.

Serving as the main hub of Contemporary Now, Lalit Kala Akademi brings together works ranging from charcoal on fabric to recycled teak wood, hand-spun textiles, digital video, and photography; the exhibition showcases artists working across a range of materials and mediums. Among the highlights are works by Anju Dodiya, Jitish Kallat, Mithu Sen, Nikhil Chopra, Raghava KK, Thukral and Tagra, Manas Udayakumar and more, each bringing their own visual vocabulary to a show that invites viewers to slow down, look closely and engage with their stories.

Ashvita’s on Radha Krishnan Salai hosts Continuiverse by C Krishnaswamy, inviting viewers to reflect on our relationship with land, memory, and community through a series of sculptures. The show draws inspiration from the Ayyanar tradition of southern India where clay was shaped into guardian figures. Meanwhile, at Ashvita’s Flagship, the gallery’s new Chennai space, Benitha K Perciyal presents How Long Will We Live? Or When Will We Die? — an exhibition that pairs her artworks with the books, research, and objects that have shaped her artistic practice and way of seeing.

Collectors choice

“Contemporary Now is built around the collector. Buying art isn’t an impulse purchase; you’re asking someone to invest anywhere between ₹5 lakh and ₹15 lakh in a work. So our job is to give them confidence. We have brought together the best galleries and artists, and every artwork sold through Contemporary Now comes with a year of art insurance, along with digital authentication and registration. We want collecting art to feel as secure and transparent as any other serious investment,” says Ashvin E Rajagopalan, director, Ashvita’s and Contemporary Now.

Madras Abstraction, presented by Gallery Veda as part of Contemporary Now, traces the evolution of abstraction through the lens of the Madras Art Movement that started in the 1960s, pioneered by DP Roy Chowdhury and KCS Paniker. Bringing together works by eight artists across generations: KV Haridasan, Achuthan Kudallur, Akkitham Narayanan, Velu Vishwanadhan, Ganesh Selvaraj, Saravanan Parasuraman, Suresh Kumar P, and Yuvan Bothysathuvar, the exhibition explores how a distinctly South Indian visual language emerged from the intersection of regional history, spirituality and modernist thought. For the event, the artists reinterpret abstraction through themes of geometry, colour, memory, and philosophy, highlighting the legacy of this influential art movement.

Explore the works of some of India’s most celebrated modern masters at Masters in Madras, a group exhibition presented by Apparao Galleries and curated by Sharan Apparao. Bringing together iconic names such as MF Husain, FN Souza, SH Raza, Arpita Singh, Anjolie Ela Menon, A Ramachandran and others, the exhibition offers a rare opportunity to view landmark works spanning diverse styles and generations. Head to Apparao Galleries, Wallace Garden, on August 9, from 5pm to 7pm, for an evening celebrating the richness and evolution of modern Indian art.

Partner programmes

Alongside the exhibitions, Contemporary Now will also feature a line-up of talks and partner programmes. On August 8 at 5 pm, Ashvita’s Flagship will host The Many Lives of the Photobook: A Contemporary Lens to Publishing Practices & Shared Futures, a panel discussion with Brendan Embser, Balaji Maheshwar and Indu Antony, moderated by Shuchi Kapoor, exploring the evolving role of the photobook. Later that evening, at 7pm, Raw Mango, Teynampet, hosts On Patronage: Public Impact, Private Collections, with Anu Menda, Meha Patel, Jaiveer Johal and Siddharth Somaiya in conversation with Umah Jacob on the relationship between private collections and public culture.

Then there is I Have A Dream, a studio exhibition by George K, at the George K Studio, T Nagar. Presented by Apparao Galleries and curated by Jaiveer Johal, this partner programme offers a peek into the artist’s visual language in the space where he created most of his art.

For those interested in photography, In Dialogue with Nature, presented by the Chennai Photo Biennale Foundation and WWF-India, runs from August 8 to 22, at the Avtar Foundation for the Arts, bringing together limited-edition photographs and portfolios centred on ecology, conservation and the natural world. Also opening on August 8 is Unruly Bodies: Sighting the Body Politic from the Avtar Collection, curated by Suchitra Vijayan at Espace 24, Alliance Française of Madras. The exhibition examines how power shapes bodies, memory, identity and belonging through works from the Avtar Collection.

Over the next two weeks, the city becomes a map of conversations and discoveries, reminding us that art lives not just within white walls, but in the people, places and stories that shape a city.

Contemporary Now Edition-III starts from August 8. To know about the full schedule, follow @contemporarynow on Instagram.

World.title: Landslips kill at least 4 in northern Philippines
World.content:
Landslips in the Philippines killed four people, authorities said on Thursday (August 6, 2026), as heavy rains driven by a tropical depression raked the country's north and forced school closures.

The archipelago nation's main island Luzon has been battered by heavy rains over the past four days.

Government offices and schools were ordered closed in the capital and across a swathe of northern provinces due to the rain.

In Benguet province, a six-hour drive north of Manila, a hillside gave way and collapsed on a small restaurant on Thursday (August 6, 2026), burying three employees who had been in the kitchen.

"One is alive. Two were dead on the spot," Colonel Dionisio Bonoy of the Benguet provincial police told reporters.

"At 10:00 a.m. [0200 GMT], the survivor was retrieved. That was our priority earlier. With the help of God, we hope he survives."

The country's national disaster agency separately confirmed two others had been killed in a landslip in neighbouring Rizal province the day before.

Earlier Thursday (August 6, 2026), government meteorologist John Manalo said sustained winds were at about 55 kilometres (34 miles) per hour, as the depression, formerly Tropical Storm Kujira, moved towards the Philippine Sea.

"Severe winds can still affect most parts of the country," he warned.

"Since our land is already saturated and soaked, the potential for flooding and landslides will be higher."

The Philippines is the first major landmass facing the Pacific cyclone belt, and the archipelago is hit by an average of 20 storms and typhoons each year, putting millions of people in disaster-prone areas in a state of constant poverty.

Scientists say human-driven climate change is making extreme weather more frequent, prolonged and intense.

World.title: PM Shehbaz, CDF Munir to visit Saudi Arabia from August 6 to 8
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, alongside Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, will undertake a visit to Saudi Arabia from August 6 to 8, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Thursday.

In a weekly press briefing, FO spokesperson Tahir Andrabi said the two will be accompanied by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, who is currently in Saudi Arabia after concluding a visit to Jordan.

“During the visit, the prime minister will meet Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, and discussions will focus on consolidating the Pakistan-Saudi bilateral relationship and exchange views on areas of regional and international developments of mutual interests,” he said.

He stressed that the visit marked Pakistan’s “long-standing partnership” with Saudi Arabia, which he said was “anchored in decades of mutual trust, cooperation and brotherhood”.

Andrabi noted that while the visit was taking place amid heightened tensions in the Gulf, he said that “it will carry immense significance beyond the immediate crisis and short-term considerations”.

He added that the visit will “further strengthen bilateral relations, deepen strategic cooperation, enhance coordination on regional and international issues of mutual interest and also reinforce multilateral cooperation”.

Shortly after, an official statement regarding the visit was also issued.

The premier had last visited Saudi Arabia in April, meeting with the kingdom’s top leadership.

As the Middle East conflict has expanded across new fronts, Saudi Arabia has unveiled plans for a multinational maritime defence coalition to protect shipping and energy supply routes in the Red Sea region. Fourteen countries, including Pakistan, have voiced support for the coalition.

In July, Pakistan also endorsed Saudi Arabia’s air strikes in Iraq as an exercise of its right to self-defence. The remarks came two days after Saudi Arabia and the US carried out coordinated strikes against installations of Iraq’s Popular Mobilisation Units, accusing elements within the umbrella force of launching attacks on Saudi oil facilities.

The remarks followed Pakistan’s earlier warning after Yemen’s Houthi rebels announced a maritime blockade targeting shipping linked to Saudi Arabia. Islamabad had then described attacks on Pakistani maritime interests as a “red line”, warning that any hostile action against Pakistani-flagged vessels or commercial shipping would be treated as an attack on Pakistan.

The country also simultaneously reaffirmed its commitment to Saudi Arabia’s security and the uninterrupted flow of lawful maritime commerce through the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandeb.

Last year, Islamabad and Riyadh concluded a Strategic Mutual Defence Agree­ment, which became operational earlier this year as Pakistan simultaneously embarked on a diplomatic effort to mediate between Iran and the United States.

World.title: IHC reserves ruling on maintainability of plea challenging presidential delay in judicial appointments
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Thursday reserved its verdict on the maintainability of a plea challenging President Asif Ali Zardari’s delay in approving a summary for the appointment and confirmation of judges to various high courts.

The writ petition, filed by advocate Luqman Zafar Chaudhary through his counsel Zahid Asif Chaudhry on Wednesday, urged the court to direct the president to approve the summary forwarded by the prime minister for the appointment of 19 additional judges and the confirmation of five judges to the Islamabad, Lahore, Sindh, Balochistan and Peshawar high courts.

Justice Arbab Muhammad Tahir took up the plea on Thursday, with the counsel for the petitioner arguing that the Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP) had recommended the appointments under consideration during its meetings on July 20 and 21. He contended that the summary had reportedly not been approved by the president even after 15 days had passed.

After the JCP — which is responsible for appointing judges to the superior judiciary and is headed by Chief Justice of Pakistan Yahya Afridi — recommended the judicial appointments last month, the summary was forwarded by the prime minister to the president for assent.

The delay in presidential assent to judicial appointments has begun to affect the functioning of the superior judiciary , with the term of an additional judge of the Sindh High Court (SHC) having already expired and four additional judges of the Peshawar High Court (PHC) facing a similar situation within days.

The petitioner’s counsel told the court that according to the available information, the government might issue notifications for the appointments in the next 48 hours.

During the hearing, the contents of his client’s plea were also read out on the court’s direction, and Justice Tahir repeatedly questioned if a constitutional petition could be maintained against the president. He asked the counsel to cite any precedent in which a writ had been issued against the president.

The court also observed that the judgements cited by the petitioner did not support the proposition advanced by his counsel for the court to issue directives to the president and asked the lawyer to identify any decision in which a court had issued directions to the president regarding the exercise of powers under Article 48 of the Constitution.

Article 48 of the Constitution states that the president shall act “on and in accordance with the advice of the cabinet or the prime minister”. However, it adds, the president can ask the cabinet or the prime minister to reconsider the advice within 15 days of receiving it and shall act in accordance with the advice tendered after reconsideration within 10 days.

For his part, the petitioner’s lawyer said that usually, the notifications for the judicial appointments were issued by the law ministry after the president’s approval. But, he contended, the law ministry could also issue the notification without the president’s approval and that the president’s role in the process was ceremonial.

The lawyer argued that once the JCP nominated judges for appointment or confirmation, the summary was sent to the president through the prime minister.

The president had no discretion beyond granting approval, and if the approval was withheld, the competent authority should proceed with issuing the notification, he contended.

Justice Tahir, however, continued to question the legal basis for issuing a writ against the president and asked the counsel to identify the competent authority responsible for issuing appointment notifications.

The counsel reiterated the law ministry was the competent authority and requested the court to seek responses from the federation, the Prime Minister’s Office and the law ministry regarding the status of the summary for the judicial appointments.

After hearing his arguments, the court declined the request to issue notices at this stage and reserved its decision on the maintainability of the petition.

More to follow

World.title: 'Growing pattern of media curbs': HRCP, PFUJ express concern over new rules for foreign press
World.content:
The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) and the Pakistan Federal Union of Journalists (PFUJ) have expressed concerns regarding media freedom after the government mandated foreign media personnel to seek permission for travelling to any city outside Islamabad, Lahore and Karachi for news coverage.

“The requirement that journalists obtain state approval to report from large parts of the country sends a chilling message: that critical reporting is unwelcome,” HRCP noted in a statement on Wednesday about the ‘Foreign Media Facilitation Guidelines 2026’.

Expressing its deep concern, the commission said the rules would “invariably institutionalise bureaucratic control over news gathering and risk deterring independent reporting on matters of public interest” rather than facilitate journalism.

“This is the latest in a growing pattern of restrictions on media freedom in Pakistan. From arbitrary curbs on reporting and increasing censorship to legal and administrative barriers, the space for independent journalism has continued to shrink,” the rights body highlighted.

It urged the government to withdraw the “restrictive measures and uphold its constitutional and international obligation to protect freedom of expression”.

Similarly, PFUJ “strongly condemned” the new rules and termed them as restrictions on press freedom.

In a statement issued on Thursday, PFUJ President Afzal Butt and Secretary General Arshad Ansari said the guidelines amount to “attacking the freedom of expression and putting curbs on press freedom”.

“The government has not only banned foreign journalists from visiting most of the areas of Pakistan except major cities, but they have also restricted the movement of Pakistani media persons working with international media outlets. They are not allowed to visit these areas on their own either,” it pointed out.

“How can foreign correspondents and their Pakistani colleagues perform their professional duties after this notification?” the PFUJ leaders asked.

They further asserted that the move would “only bring disrepute to Pakistan and damage its image”.

The PFUJ statement noted, “Pakistan is already ranked very low among the countries that have the worst record in press freedom. And the action of the government would add to it.”

It demanded that the government immediately “lift this ban” if it believed in democracy and press freedom, arguing that such a move would also impact the employment of Pakistanis working with international media outlets.

“Naturally, if Pakistani journalists working with global media outlets are unable to visit different areas, it means they would not be able to perform their professional responsibilities. Consequently, they would lose their jobs,” it contended.

The PFUJ leaders were quoted as saying that such actions “are taken in banana republics, not in countries that claim to follow democratic principles”.

“If the demands of PFUJ are not accepted, we would be left with no option but to resort to protest and demonstrations,” it warned.

According to the new guidelines, all foreign media personnel will now need a no-objection certificate (NOC) from the information ministry to travel to any city except Islamabad, Lahore and Karachi to produce “news content, story, video, film, documentary or social media content” for official use.

Additionally, under the new rules, all entities operating in Pakistan to facilitate foreign media “in any capacity” are also required to register with the ministry’s External Publicity (EP) Wing, as are non-journalists living in Pakistan who render services to foreign media.

The guidelines also specify that individuals’ press registration can be suspended or withdrawn for “acts against ideology, sovereignty, security or public order of Pakistan”, and if the EP Wing “deems appropriate at any stage”.

World.title: IHC restrains NCCIA from harassing journalist Asad Toor during inquiry
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Thursday restrained the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) from harassing vlogger and journalist Asad Toor during the course of its inquiry.

The agency had issued a notice to Toor on July 29 for an inquiry into “alleged dissemination, transmission and/or public exhibition of false/fake information” by him. He was directed to appear before the NCCIA Cybercrime Reporting Centre in Islamabad at 11am on July 31.

Toor had challenged the summons in the IHC the following day, arguing that the NCCIA had failed to fulfil the legal requirements while issuing the notice and had not provided details of the allegations against him.

The court had subsequently directed the agency to provide Toor with details of the allegations against him; his counsel argued that the agency had not specified the accusations, making it impossible for him to respond to the inquiry.

On Thursday, Justice Khadim Hussain Soomro heard the petition. During the proceedings, the petitioner’s counsel, Advocate Attaullah Kundi, said that Toor was willing to join the inquiry but feared being arrested.

“We want to appear in the inquiry, but we do not want to be arrested,” the counsel told the court, adding that allegations of disseminating fake and false information had been levelled against the journalist.

Justice Khadim Hussain Soomro asked the petitioner’s counsel which particular news report had been described as fake. In response, Advocate Kundi stated that the allegation related to a news report concerning the medical condition of the PTI founder.

After hearing the arguments, the court directed that Toor should not be harassed during the inquiry. It also summoned the investigating officer in his personal capacity and adjourned further proceedings in the case.

Last month, the National Press Club (NPC) had condemned the NCCIA notice to Toor, expressing alarm at the state of press freedom.

Asserting that the right to freedom of expression was a constitutional right, NPC leadership said, “Subjecting journalists to legal pressure and retaliation for performing their professional duties or expressing critical opinions is not a good omen for any democratic society.”

World.title: Ex-Bangladesh cricket captain Shakib's home attacked after joining Hasina's first public media event since ouster
World.content:
Windows were smashed and petrol bombs hurled at former Bangladesh cricket captain Shakib Al Hasan’s residence after he joined ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina’s first public media interaction since her 2024 removal from power, in which she vowed to return in December.

Police said a group of people attacked Shakib’s ancestral home in Magura town, about 170 km (105 miles) southwest of the capital Dhaka on Wednesday, causing a fire on the upper floor of the residence. The property was unoccupied at the time and no injuries were reported.

The attack came hours after Shakib, a former Awami League lawmaker, joined a virtual event organised by the Foreign Correspondents Club of South Asia in New Delhi. During the audio address, Hasina reiterated that she would return to Bangladesh, where she has been sentenced to death.

Shakib, who was elected to parliament as an Awami League candidate in January 2024, has remained outside Bangladesh since the student-led uprising that toppled Hasinas government. He faces multiple investigations, including over allegations of murder, embezzlement, fraud and money laundering.

“I will return to my people,” Hasina said. “I know that they may put me in jail or they may kill me, but still I have to go back.”

The event, held on the second anniversary of her ouster, was Hasina’s first public interaction with the media since she fled Bangladesh in 2024. Hasina also said the ban on the Awami League, the party she led for more than four decades, should be lifted after it was barred from political activity following her ouster.

Bangladesh’s foreign ministry condemned Hasina’s media appearance, describing it as an affront to the sovereignty of Bangladesh and warning that allowing her to address the media from India could harm bilateral relations.

Hasina, 78, has been living in New Delhi since August 2024. Bangladesh has sought her extradition from India, which says the request is being examined under its legal procedures.

In November 2025, the country’s war crimes tribunal sentenced her to death in absentia over the deadly crackdown on the 2024 student-led uprising, charges she has dismissed as politically motivated.

World.title: US firms look to Pakistan for critical mineral supplies
World.content:
• Smaller mines and larger copper, antimony projects under consideration

• US Embassy official says Reko Diq moving forward, but slower than expected

• Encourages Pakistan to provide level playing field to American firms

• Finance minister, US trade representative review progress on bilateral trade talks

ISLAMABAD: Amid a big push from the Trump administration to secure global critical mineral supply chains, US companies are exploring opportunities to take over and develop smaller mines in Pakistan, besides looking at more significant investments in larger projects, potentially in copper and other critical minerals such as antimony.

Speaking to journalists at a background briefing, a US Embassy official said the Trump administration had been focusing on critical mineral supply chains around the world, particularly in Pakistan, through multilateral agencies, the US International Development Finance Corporation and the Export-Import Bank of the United States.

The official said the US Exim Bank had committed $1.25 billion for the Reko Diq copper-gold project in Balochistan, though financing terms were still being finalised.

The remarks coincided with Pakistan-US discussions on bilateral trade at a virtual meeting between Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb and US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer to review progress on negotiations for a bilateral trade agreement.

The Ministry of Finance said Mr Aurangzeb and Mr Greer noted that negotiations on the proposed reciprocal trade framework had advanced significantly and reaffirmed their shared commitment to concluding the agreement at the earliest.

The US Embassy in Islamabad and the administration in Washington have been working with American companies to explore investment opportunities in Pakistan, including trade operations to buy offtakes from small mines in Pakistan for use or processing in the United States, the official said.

The US Embassy official said some products could also be supplied by US firms to supply chains in Germany, South Korea and elsewhere.

The official said Pakistan possessed many critical minerals, including big antimony concentrations, though not large deposits like Reko Diq. Some of the roughly 60 critical minerals were found in Pakistan and were important for aircraft manufacturing, semiconductors, defence equipment in the US and other supply chains, he said.

He said Pakistan-US cooperation in these areas could be beneficial for both sides, adding that Washington was pushing for investment and bilateral trade to process those minerals in the US.

The official said Pakistan’s mineral sector was currently contributing about 3pc to the national GDP, while Reko Diq alone could add another 0.5pc to GDP.

He said a number of US companies were currently engaged with Pakistani authorities and companies to develop critical mineral mines, as the Trump administration was focused on ensuring stronger supply chains for national defence and industry.

He avoided discussing specifics, saying the companies would make announcements themselves as agreements materialised.

Responding to a question on whether the multibillion-dollar Reko Diq project was currently on pause, the US Embassy official said the project was moving forward, though slower than originally planned.

He said financial institutions, including the International Finance Corporation and others, were currently discussing financing.

“The project is so large that it cannot be expected to move according to the original plan and not to change,” he said.

The official said the US had been encouraging Pakistan to provide a level playing field to American companies and strengthen local institutions such as the Geological Survey of Pakistan to carry out feasibility studies so that US firms could identify investment opportunities.

He acknowledged that the Pakistan government was doing whatever it could to facilitate US companies as well as other global firms. However, he stressed that investment could not flow without removing red tape.

The official said that US Strategic Metals had exported a mineral consignment supplied by the Frontier Works Organisation, which was being processed in the US, and both sides were looking at more trade and investment opportunities.

Responding to a question about US-China competition for mineral sector investments, the official said that in Pakistan’s context, it was not a matter of the US or China.

He said Pakistan was looking for investment from around the world, including in critical minerals, and this provided opportunities not only to Chinese and US firms but also to companies from Australia, Canada and other countries, which could also help train the local workforce.

Responding to a question on the security situation in Balochistan, he said security challenges were real, but opportunities also existed because of highly prospective mineral deposits.

He said people in the industry understood those challenges and knew how to navigate them, given the high returns from rich natural deposits in areas such as Chitral, which could have successful antimony operations, and Waziristan, where copper concentrations had been found. He said similar potential existed in Gilgit-Baltistan and Balochistan.

Over the past year, the Trump administration has been seeking to build secure and transparent mineral supply chains for American industry amid Washington’s growing concerns over China’s edge in global rare earth materials.

Pakistan has been trying to balance renewed momentum in Pakistan-US trade and economic ties with its long-term friendly relations with China.

US stakeholders are concerned about China’s growing control over global critical minerals, believing that Chinese dominance stems from government subsidies, vertical integration and lax regulations, in contrast to US underinvestment.

The US administration considers critical minerals foundational to the modern economy and state power, and essential for advanced technologies in energy, military and commercial applications, ranging from permanent magnets in fighter jets to batteries in electric vehicles.

Published in Dawn, August 6th, 2026

World.title: Govt will complete tenure, Shehbaz to remain PM for five years: Naqvi
World.content:
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Wednesday said the incumbent government would complete its constitutional term and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif would remain in office for the full five-year tenure.

Naqvi made the remarks while speaking to the media outside the Interior Ministry in Islamabad, a week after saying the country’s governance system had “collapsed” and arguing that Pakistan needed new administrative units, or provinces, to improve service delivery, accountability and access to justice.

A day later, the military’s spokesperson also called on political parties to consider an administrative reset to improve governance, arguing that the country’s security and stability depended on adapting its governance structure to the demands of modern times and a growing population.

“The future for the government is the completion of its five-year tenure … Shehbaz sahib will remain the prime minister for five years … the prime minister will complete his five-year term,” Naqvi said on Wednesday.

When asked whether his remarks about the “collapse” of the system amounted to a “charge sheet” against the government, Naqvi said he stood by his statement, maintaining that “the system has been destroyed”.

He clarified that he was referring to the country’s “80-year-old [administrative] system”.

“Even today, I maintain that the system that has been in place for the last 80 years is destroyed, because if it had been functioning, Pakistan would have reached new heights,” he said.

Naqvi clarified that he had not “charge-sheeted” the government, saying he himself was part of the same administration.

“If you have a prime minister who works 14 to 16 hours a day, and if the current situation improves, the results will be a thousand times better,” he said.

Elaborating on the achievements of the prime minister and the incumbent government, the interior minister said that the Federal Board of Revenue’s (FBR) revenue had increased manifold, Pakistan had won a war against India, its diplomatic standing had improved significantly worldwide, and numerous reforms had been introduced.

“I still believe today that if the prime minister had operated within a better system, he could have taken this country forward a hundred times more,” Naqvi said, while highlighting the efforts made by the premier.

He also briefly referred to certain individuals who wanted to create differences between him and Shehbaz.

Naqvi’s earlier remarks had sparked a political controversy, drawing criticism from government allies, opposition parties and other political figures.

Responding to the interior minister’s call for an overhaul of the country’s governance structure, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif advised him to begin the process by implementing the National Action Plan (NAP) and bringing reforms to his own ministry.

Asif further noted that Naqvi had held a “very powerful position” in the system for the past three years.

The PPP also demanded the resignation of Naqvi, accusing him of undermining the Constitution by “endorsing a hybrid system”, declaring that the country’s democratic system of governance had collapsed and calling for the creation of new provinces .

Meanwhile, former Senate chairman Mian Raza Rabbani strongly opposed the proposal to create new provinces, arguing that Pakistan’s governance failures stem from violations of the Constitution rather than the existing federating units.

In a detailed statement, he cautioned that redrawing administrative boundaries would not resolve the country’s deep-rooted systemic issues. Instead, he said, the real causes of the governance crisis are the erosion of provincial autonomy and the weakening of democratic institutions.

Naqvi’s controversial remarks came on the same day that he met President Asif Ali Zardari at Bilawal House, where they reviewed “the country’s overall law and order situation, with a particular focus on security conditions in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan.

World.title: New US policy gives officials more power to reject immigration filings
World.content:
WASHINGTON: Immigrants seeking work permits, green cards, or changes of status could face a greater risk of having their applications denied under a new US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) policy that took effect on August 5.

The policy, announced by USCIS on Wednesday, gives immigration officials broader discretion to deny incomplete applications without first allowing applicants an opportunity to submit missing documents or other required evidence.

The new policy applies to a wide range of applications handled by USCIS, including those for green cards, work permits, US citizenship, travel documents, and other immigration-related approvals.

Under the revised guidance, applicants must prove they qualify for the immigration status or approval they are seeking and submit all required supporting documents when they file their application.

If they fail to do so, USCIS officers may deny the application without first issuing a request for evidence (RFE) or a notice of intent to deny (NOID), both of which previously allowed applicants to correct mistakes or provide missing documents.

USCIS said the change restores officers’ discretion under long-standing Department of Homeland Security regulations and reverses a Biden-era policy that generally encouraged officers to request additional evidence before denying an incomplete application.

According to the agency, the previous policy allowed some people to file incomplete or “placeholder” applications to obtain temporary immigration advantages, such as work authorisation while waiting to submit the required evidence. It said the new policy will help reduce frivolous filings, improve efficiency, and shorten processing times for applicants who submit complete applications.

For many South Asian immigrants, the change could have important practical consequences, as they account for a large number of family-sponsored and employment-based immigration applications. Many also apply for work permits, adjustment of status to permanent residence, naturalisation, and other immigration services provided by USCIS.

Immigration lawyers say these applications often require extensive documentation. Under the new policy, forgetting to include a required document or failing to demonstrate eligibility at the time of filing is more likely to result in an immediate denial.

However, the policy does not change who qualifies for a green card, work permit, citizenship or any other immigration status.

The updated policy applies to immigration applications that were pending or filed on or after Aug 5 unless a specific law or USCIS regulation provides otherwise.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies.
